Sports.title: Why Joshua Zirkzee might have a future at Man United after all, how Shea Lacey stole the show and the kids shine again: THINGS WE LEARNED as Michael Carrick's men thrash Rosenborg
Sports.content:
Manchester United bounced back from an opening pre-season defeat by Wrexham in Helsinki last weekend by thumping Rosenborg 5-0 in the Lerkendal Stadion in Trondheim.

Head coach Michael Carrick again started with a strong line-up against a side who are 13 games into the Norwegian League season, and the majority of his starting XI stayed on the pitch for an hour as United took a two-goal lead through Shea Lacey and an audacious effort from Joshua Zirkzee.

Carrick then sent on his youngsters who seized the opportunity to impress for the second game in a row and scored three more through Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams.

Perhaps the only disappointment for the United fans in Norway was that teenage star JJ Gabriel didn’t get on the pitch after he was included in the first-team squad for the first time.

Still, there is plenty of excitement to be taken from Friday evening's match.

The Daily Mail Sport looks at what we learned from United’s second pre-season game as Carrick and his players head home from Trondheim ahead of the next friendly against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm a week on Saturday.

Joshua Zirkzee showed why he could still have a Manchester United future with a fine goal

It came as Michael Carrick's side thumped Rosenborg 5-0 in their second pre-season friendly

Zirkzee’s timely reminder

Zirkzee has faced his fair share of criticism since moving to Old Trafford two years ago. The Dutchman has struggled to live up to expectations, and it has never been clear just where he fitted in under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick.

With United keen to bring in support for striker Benjamin Sesko this summer, they would listen to offers for Zirkzee, but the former Bologna player showed what he can do in Trondheim with a standout display in the win over Rosenborg.

Having set up Bryan Mbeumo for an early chance, he got the assist on Lacey’s opening goal just after the half hour mark. But Zirkzee saved the best for himself in the 56th minute after he started a move from halfway with a pass out to Amass on the left.

The young full-back played the ball back to him, and Zirkzee sold one dummy to bamboozle the Norwegians’ defence and another to leave goalkeeper Rasmus Sandberg on his backside before scoring in an empty net.

For all his critics, Zirkzee possesses the touch and trickery that many players don’t. He just needs to produce an end product on a more consistent basis against the better teams. Maybe he could have a future at Old Trafford yet.

Show-stopper Shea

The talk beforehand had been about the prospect of JJ Gabriel’s first-team debut, but Lacey showed once again what an exciting young prospect he is with an excellent performance in Norway.

The 19-year-old from Liverpool made an immediate impact for the senior side when he got a chance off the bench at Aston Villa in December and rattled the bar as United went in search of an equaliser, but saw his development cruelly cut short when he was handed another opportunity by caretaker boss Darren Fletcher in the FA Cup defeat by Brighton in January when he was sent off for two bookable offences.

However, Lacey re-appeared on the final day, against Brighton again, and he showed his determination to kick on this season after being selected in the senior side that stayed largely unchanged for an hour in Trondheim.

Shea Lacey caused Rosenborg all sorts of problems starting in the No10 role on Friday

Operating primarily in the No10 role behind Zirkzee, Lacey caused Rosenborg all sorts of problems by floating into the pockets and supporting Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu on the flanks.

Moments after playing a part in the move that ended with Dorgu firing just wide of the far post, he put United ahead with a coolly-taken goal. It began on the edge of United’s box with Ayden Heaven who fed Zirkzee, and his pass set Lacey en route to goal.

The youngster was being carefully marshalled by Tomas Nemcik, but cut inside the Rosenborg centre-back and beat goalkeeper Leopold Wahlstedt by guiding the ball inside the far post.

Kids shine again

United’s youngsters followed up a promising performance in Helsinki with an even better display in Trondheim as right back Jaydan Kamason emerged as the pick of the bunch with two assists.

After Devaney had scored from close-range at a corner, Kamason made an overlap on the right before finding Amass who stretched out a leg to score at the back post in the 67th minute. He then tricked his way to the byline to thread another cross to the feet of Williams who tapped in six minutes from the end.

Rosenborg may have made nine changes at half-time and more as the second half progressed in preparation for their next game against Fredrikstad on Monday, but Carrick was delighted with the way United’s kids performed.

‘The younger players came on in the second half, and I thought they were fantastic,’ said the United boss. ‘They played as a team really well and deserved what they got.

‘When you see them expressing themselves and pushing themselves to be better, I was delighted to see that from them. They’ve all got potential in different ways, and you want them to fulfil it and they certainly did that. Some of the goals were fantastic goals, and it was just as pleasing to keep the clean sheet.’

Jaydan Kamason (right) was the pick of the young players that shone as he picked up two assists from right back

Stars are fighting fit

The next game against Atletico Madrid will be a step up for United, and Carrick built his players’ fitness by giving most of them an hour in Trondheim after playing 45 minutes against Wrexham.

Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw went off at the interval, and eight more of the starting XI followed after 60 minutes. Goalkeeper Radek Vitek – one of two changes from Helsinki along with Shea Lacey – stayed on for 70 minutes and was hardly tested aside from one effort that clipped the bar before he was replaced by Dermot Mee.

‘It was a good day,’ said Carrick afterwards. ‘A clean sheet and we scored goals. By the looks of it, everyone coming through injury free is what you want at this stage. I think keeping players fit and progressing through pre-season is as important as anything.

‘Some players need more minutes than others as they go. You're managing some players a little bit more than others. It's never going to be perfect with two weeks in.

‘I think we're in a good place. Four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress. Moving forward, it's a really good direction to go in.’

Sports.title: Como set to make improved bid for Chelsea's Trevoh Chalobah... with Blues holding out for £35m including add-ons
Sports.content:
Como are expected to hold talks with Chelsea on Saturday over an improved offer for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The England centre back is keen on making the move and the Italians - managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas - have indicated they would increase their bid closer to Chelsea's valuation of £35million including add-ons.

Como have so far proposed £25m.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month how Fabregas wants Chalobah at his Serie A club for next season.

Trevoh Chalobah was a late call-up for England's World Cup squad after Tino Livramento was forced to withdraw

Como were rebuffed in their opening two proposals for the 27-year-old and have been working to meet Chelsea's valuation with a structured offer.

Inter Milan have also discussed Chalobah as they want two centre backs but Como are hopeful they can conclude a deal.

Chelsea are closing in on a £55m deal for Crystal Palace centre hal Maxence Lacroix, who is having his medical today

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Sports.title: Hulk Hogan's son reflects on 'very difficult year' in emotional tribute to WWE legend on anniversary of his death
Sports.content:
Hulk Hogan's son paid an emotional tribute to his late father on the anniversary of the wrestling legend's death.

Former WWE star Hulk - born Terry Gene Bollea - died at 71 one year ago on July 24, 2025, after suffering cardiac arrest at his mansion in Clearwater, Florida, leaving the wrestling world grieving.

One year on, his son, Nick, commemorated the anniversary of the death of his 'best friend, mentor and most importantly, father.'

Nick reflected on the 'very difficult year,' admitting that 'not a single day goes by that I don’t wish I could have him back' for one more hug, laugh or conversation.

'With the pain that comes with feeling this deep of loss, my perspective has changed,' wrote in an Instagram post on Friday.

'Legacy is not just the memories you leave behind or the things that you accomplish in your lifetime. It’s also what you inspire others to do and how you affect everyone who comes into your life.

Hulk Hogan's son paid an emotional tribute to his late father on the anniversary of his death

The wrestling legend died at the age of 71 from cardiac arrest on July 24, 2025

'I can say that my father was the best at that and his legacy is unrivaled.'

He continued: 'The lives he touched and inspiration he gave the world reaches far beyond any one moment in time. It was his life’s work and he continues to inspire me to make each day intentional. To become the best version of myself and a man that I know he would be proud of.

'My father is not just the greatest wrestler of all time but also, the best dad a guy could have ever had. I am so grateful and blessed to have had him as my dad and to have the honor of being his son. I will always cherish the memories, lessons and values that he gave me and start each day with the purpose and intention to use them to the best of my ability.'

'I will love and miss him every single day of my life and carry him with me in my heart until I see him again,' he concluded.

The Clearwater Police Department officially closed its investigation into Hulk's death in June, releasing a comprehensive 72-page report that details the definitive timeline inside his Florida estate.

According to the files, Hogan - born Terry Gene Bollea - had been quietly fighting private health battles against both chronic lymphocytic leukemia and atrial fibrillation, a serious heart rhythm condition, neither of which had been publicly disclosed.

On the morning of his passing, caregivers noted that the larger-than-life superstar was 'a little mumbly' but managed to get out of bed, speak with staff, and eat a breakfast of yogurt and fresh berries.

The situation deteriorated rapidly shortly after breakfast when his occupational therapist, Justin McCamey, went to check the multi-time world champion's vitals and realized he had completely stopped breathing.

Nick commemorated the anniversary his 'best friend, mentor and most importantly, father'

He shared a touching social media post on Instagram with a series of photos of his father

First responders rushed to the Clearwater residence following a frantic cardiac arrest dispatch call, but the standard lifesaving measures were ultimately unsuccessful and Hogan was pronounced dead at a nearby hospital.

'He is in rough shape,' McCamey told a responding officer at the scene immediately following the medical emergency. 'We knew this was gonna be happening.'

After a thorough review of internal home surveillance footage, medical histories and extensive interviews with his dedicated care team, detectives officially ruled the tragedy an attended natural death caused by a heart attack.

The finality of the police report brings a somber sense of closure to millions of fans worldwide who grew up worshiping 'Hulkamania,' the pop culture craze that transformed pro wrestling into a mainstream global phenomenon.

Brooke Hogan, Hulk's daughter, shared an estranged relationship with her father before his death.

Earlier this year, sheissued a furious response to 'trolls' who criticized her for posting a tribute to her late father while posing in a bikini.

Brooke took to Instagram to share a series of photos of her dad, in light of his tragic death. However, a number of users took aim at Brooke for starting the post with a picture of herself laying face down on the beach in a bikini.

The WWE star collapsed at his Florida home before being pronounced dead at the hospital

Recently, at the end of May, Hogan's estranged daughter Brooke issued a furious response to 'trolls' who criticized her for posting a tribute to her late father while posing in a bikini

In light of the reaction, Brooke fired back at her critics in another post on Instagram, which starts with edited snaps of her body looking less flattering on the beach.

'Would my post have been more sincere if THIS girl were at the beach mourning her dad?' she asked.

Brooke also added: 'I took one photo over my shoulder quickly... and proceeded to google why I'm so emotionally fatigued immediately after... And then I spent an hour looking at and saving pictures of my dad.'

Her apparent intention in including the photo was to reference the ocean, where she and wrestling legend Hogan spent much of their time together as she grew up along Florida's gulf coast.

Sports.title: Revealed: Jude Bellingham's brutal dig at World Cup referee as unseen footage goes viral - moments before England star slapped Argentina rival following semi-final defeat
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed.

The Real Madrid star made a point of confronting Ismail Elfath – Lionel Messi's favourite referee – to share his grievances after England's 2-1 loss last week.

Argentina employed roughhouse tactics against England, committing 15 fouls, to book their place in the final against Spain, where they lost 1-0.

Leandro Paredes and Enzo Fernandez were seen as particularly dirty in the opening exchanges of the match.

Both teams came into the match with a heightened sense of rivalry after the South American side's declarations throughout the tournament that the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina.

Fresh footage from the referee's camera has been released by FIFA and in it, Bellingham is seen saying to the referee: 'Some shocking ones there, but all the best.'

Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed

He was annoyed at decisions that had gone in Argentina's favour in their tense encounter

Bellingham, who scored seven goals for the Three Lions at the tournament, later slapped Argentina rival Valentin Barco on the back of the head as scenes turned ugly in Atlanta.

In the build-up to the flashpoint, Spurs captain and Argentina defender Cristian Romero was seen goading Bellingham when the final whistle was blown.

He went over to Barco and slapped him on the back of the head.

The full-back then turned around and pushed Bellingham with tempers flaring. Nicolas Otamendi also came over and gave the England man a shove.

Several Argentine players attempted to act as peacemakers, but it looked as if Bellingham and Otamendi wanted more head-to-head action – even when they were separated.

During the celebrations Argentina's stars held aloft a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

Despite FIFA's ban on political flags, Romero, Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and ex-Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso celebrated with the controversial sign after the final whistle.

Captain and star player Lionel Messi was also seen dancing alongside the banner.

Join the discussion Has Messi’s and Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup tarnished their legacy in football?

Bellingham was goaded by Argentina star Cristian Romero at the final whistle

The midfielder also clashed with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco after the semi-final

Bellingham appeared to slap new Chelsea man Barco on the back of the head

He was also at loggerheads with defender Nicolas Otamendi as other players tried to stop them

FIFA are already looking into disciplinary action relating to the banner and Argentina's behaviour following their loss to Spain in the final.

The South American side's dirty tactics against England, plus the consistent allegations throughout the tournament that things were 'rigged' in their favour, have not done Messi's popularity any favours on these shores.

Messi is now viewed unfavourably among almost half of the participants surveyed by YouGov.

After losing 1-0 to Spain some of the Argentina squad started fights with the Spanish players. Fernandez was sent off in normal time and Paredes was lambasted for attacking Eric Garcia and Gavi after the match.

Even Messi was dragged into their pathetic antics in the final, attempting to get Marc Cucurella sent off for briefly putting his hand over his mouth.

Messi also clashed with Bellingham in the semi-finals, though England fans have to admit that the legend was brilliant towards the end of the match, setting up both of his country's goals.

All of this has had a deleterious effect on Messi's popularity.

Coming into the World Cup, he was viewed favourably by 55 per cent of the public and unfavourably by just nine per cent.

Now, he is seen favourably by only 29 per cent and unfavourably by 44 per cent.

That means that, according to YouGov's poll, Messi's net favourability rating among Britons has fallen from +46 to -15. In short, people don't like him very much.

His score is far worse than his arch-rival Cristiano Ronaldo, whose net rating is -2.

And he certainly lost his stock with Daily Mail Sport's veteran columnist Jeff Powell, who bunged Messi out of his top five all-time players for his antics.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games heat plunged into chaos with star's appearance delayed by 10 minutes - before volunteer strips off to save the day
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games return was marred by a bizarre delay which held him back from the pool for 10 minutes.

The swimmer, who has added his wife Holly's family surname to his own, made a splash in the 100m breaststroke heats.

Ramsay-Peaty recorded the quickest time of anybody in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals this evening, with the final being tomorrow.

But the 31-year-old, who is targeting a fifth Commonwealth gold medal, had to wait around due to a strange occurrence.

While he was on the blocks, one of the lane dividers broke off, leading to some commotion as the fixing had sunk to the bottom of the pool.

Fortunately, a volunteer was on hand to strip down to his shorts and dive in to amend the problem.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty (not pictured) was delayed on his return to the Commonwealth Games... as a volunteer had to jump in the pool to fix a lane line

The swimmer blasted through his 100m breaststroke heat and is hoping for a fifth Commonwealth gold

Holly Ramsay cheered husband Adam on from the sidelines amid her pregnancy

And none of that put Ramsay-Peaty off his stride as he blasted to a time of 59.46 seconds.

This is his fourth Commonwealth Games – his debut was in 2014 in Glasgow, and he has made the tournament a happy hunting ground with four golds and three silvers.

Alongside the 100m, the three-time Olympic champion will also partake in the 50m breaststroke event.

His wife, Holly, the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay, shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in his new 'Ramsay-Peaty' swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special.'

Holly, a 26-year-old influencer, is pregnant with their child.

Swimmer Ramsay-Peaty's parents did not attend the wedding in December and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail revealed that Adam's pregnant sister Bethany – the only member of his family to still be in contact with the couple – has now sensationally fallen out with Holly.

The roots of the family conflict go back to September 2024, when Adam and Holly snubbed wider members of the Peaty family by not inviting them to their engagement party.

Holly shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in the new swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special'

The athlete duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds

Influencer Holly, 26, announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam

His parents, Caroline and Mark, did not attend the wedding and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them

Join the discussion Could you stay focused after an unexpected delay?

Mother Caroline, who spent years ferrying her son to early-morning training sessions, was also not invited to Holly's glamorous hen do at Soho Farmhouse in the Cotswolds, even though the bride's mother, Tana, and friends including Victoria, were at the extravagant bash.

Adam changing his name to Ramsay-Peaty and registering under the double-barrel surname for the Games in Glasgow is seen by some as the latest blow for his estranged loved ones – especially as Ramsay is placed first before Peaty.

A source said previously: 'Adam may be rich but we have something that he doesn't and that is brains, loyalty, integrity and family.

'Money makes for a cold bedfellow. It can't hold you tight when things go wrong or when you have a bad day.'

They added: 'When you live to be famous you aren't living, you are playing a role. Fame is fleeting but family is forever.'

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

He credits his Christian faith with saving him and helping him turn his life around.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

The athlete, who is due to return for his semi-final on Friday evening, told TNT Sports: 'Job done, really. We've got a busy two weeks coming up, so we're reserving energy where we can.

'Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it's been a very long journey.'

Sports.title: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers as NBA icon finally makes a decision on his future
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LeBron James has stunned the NBA by signing with the Philadelphia 76ers.

It ends the uncertainty over the NBA icon's future that has dominated the offseason and brings his spell with the Los Angeles Lakers to an end after an eight-season run highlighted by the 2020 NBA title.

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey as he pursues an elusive fifth NBA title.

He is set to sign a modest $8 million, two-year contract with the Sixers, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

In a lengthy statement on X, the 41-year-old admitted he strongly considered retiring but believes he still has 'more to give' and can turn his new team into a contender.

He wrote: 'I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game.

LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal

The 41-year-old, pictured with wife Savannah, has spent the summer deciding his future

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown

'I still truly love this game, and I have more to give. The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.

'This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.

'I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!'

James told the Lakers earlier this summer that he would not be returning to Los Angeles next season.

Reports claimed that James' former teams, the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Miami Heat, were leading the charge to sign him. He was also heavily linked to the Golden State Warriors.

But James joins a 76ers team that has not won an NBA championship since 1983 and has not advanced out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs since 2001.

Philadelphia fans will be hoping he can wipe out that streak just as he did in Cleveland, who had not won a title for 52 years before he led them to success in 2016.

The Athletic reports that Maxey and other key figures with Philadelphia have been relentlessly pursuing James in recent weeks. Their blockbuster trade for Brown with the Celtics also tipped the balance in their favor.

James, who will turn 42 in December, is about to enter his 24th season in the NBA, which is a league record. He is the all-time leading scorer in NBA history and has won four championships, two with the Heat and once each with the Cavaliers and Lakers.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton is back at the scene of his career nadir - 12 months on, it's time to prove he CAN still hit the heights of his prime, writes JONATHAN McEVOY
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is back at the scene of his career nadir - 12 months on, it's time to prove he CAN still hit the heights of his prime, writes JONATHAN McEVOY

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It’s the place and the time for Lewis Hamilton to show he can still hit the high notes of his operatic prime.

Of all the tracks where he has excelled the Hungaroring sits high on the shortlist of his favourites, along with Silverstone, Shanghai and Montreal. He has won here eight times, more than anyone else. And this weekend, the second corner, a right-hand kink, has been named in his honour.

Friday's data from practice offered him rich hope. He topped allcomers, 0.148sec in front of his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc.

All of which evidence, ancient and modern, makes it all the more surprising that last year this was the scene of the lowest point of Hamilton’s career, a trough so deep it seemed he might walk away from the sport.

‘Completely useless,’ was his self-diagnosis after watching Leclerc take pole as he qualified a flaccid 12th. The disparity typified a malaise that persisted all season.

Speaking on his return to Budapest, he referenced that dejecting nadir, saying: ‘I’m really proud of everyone in the team and of myself for digging us out of the hole I was in.

It's time for Lewis Hamilton to show he can still perform at his best as he chases an eighth World Championship

‘One day when I release my documentary, I’ll reveal everything about that weekend and what led to what happened.’

While we await that revelation, it can be stated clearly that he is in markedly better spirits and form 12 months on. His win in Barcelona in June, his first for Ferrari, is testament to this.

His upturn, in a car much better suited to his driving style, makes him the nearest challenger to Kimi Antonelli, the 19-year-old protégé who replaced him at Mercedes. Hamilton is 45 points back from the Italian going into the 11th round of the season, the final instalment before Formula One’s summer break.

Ah, fine and way better than the whole of his first campaign with Ferrari, but he is still to show he can reach the peaks every week necessary to add the eighth world title he craves as the final brushstroke to his self-described masterpiece.

Yes, he outscored Leclerc by 53 points in the five races leading up to Silverstone. But Leclerc has held the edge since then. The Monegasque won the British race, two places ahead of Hamilton. Ditto two places ahead in Spa last weekend. Leclerc was also fastest in those two qualifying sessions.

The Hamilton of old would, surely, have had the measure of Leclerc – who is dramatically fast but prone to mistakes under emotion – over the course of a long season when the title is at stake. He well might again but still has to prove he can at the age of 41.

So to this weekend’s opportunity. First thing to say, Ferrari are favourites for the win. Their shortcomings, such as they are, lie in their relative lack of engine power and their strengths in aerodynamic alacrity through corners. The twisty Hungaroring, with just one decent straight, plays to their areas of potency.

To elaborate on the practice charts that support the theory of red ascendancy, Leclerc was fastest in the first session by half-a-second over Hamilton before the British veteran turned it around in the second go, 0.148sec ahead.

He returns to the location of one of the worst days in his career, coming last year

In further good news, the Mercedes pair of Antonelli and George Russell, who is five points back from Hamilton, were off the pace and visibly struggling. They ended up fifth and 13th. Their prospects of maintaining their record of pole in every round this season are slim.

In passing, if it is a big weekend for Hamilton, the same is true for Russell. He speaks with calm assurance as setback after setback assails him. His verbal resilience is admirable but he needs to assert himself over Antonelli on track, and fast, to dispel a nagging fear that his championship hopes are dripping down the windowpane, drop by drop.

Whose nagging fears? His own mostly, one suspects, for all his bullish words. His confidence has not expired but lies in intensive care.

He is helped in his task by the fact the technical gremlins that blighted him in Spa have been resolved by his Mercedes brainboxes in the intervening days.

Away from the top, Aston Martin have brought a raft of upgrades to Hungary. My, they need them after what the team’s star designer Adrian Newey admitted had been a ‘complete nightmare’ season.

The green shoots were, well, patchy. They clawed back some time relative to their previous sluggishness in the first practice session before Lance Stroll’s suspension failed him. Oh dear.

Stroll sat out the rest of the day, while Fernando Alonso was 19th, 2.9sec off the pace. Newey talked of ‘respectability’ being their target in the mid-term, aware that loftier ambitions are unrealistic.

He was asked if Christian Horner might be on the way to the team. As previously reported in the Daily Mail Sport, owner Lawrence Stroll is repeatedly keen to enlist the former Red Bull boss and has returned to seek his services more than once.

Adrian Newey is remaining coy on whether Christian Horner (pictured) could join Aston Martin

Newey, team principal, is less than mad on the idea of a reunion with his old partner during their glory days together at Milton Keynes.

‘I keep hearing these rumours about Christian,’ said Newey.

‘I can’t comment further. All I can say is we are happy with our senior management team.’

Easy to say, Adrian. Papa Stroll’s judgment is subject to review. Nobody ever claimed the bluff billionaire has the patience of Job.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury fight LIVE RESULT from Anthony Joshua warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's blistering rant on the heavyweight division

Tyson Fury brutally did not hold back in his assessment of the current landscape of the heavyweight division.

Since Fury's return, the heavyweight division has changed immensely. Following Oleksandr Usyk's controversial stoppage win against kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven over in Egypt back in May, the Ukrainian decided to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has sent shockwaves across the sport.

Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Agit Kabayel is recognised as the WBC title holder. Daniel Dubois became a two-time world champion after knocking out Fabio Wardley back in May for the WBO strap, and the IBF belt remains vacant. Following the monumental shift, it now presents Fury with a perfect chance to become a three-time champion.

But when asked where he fits into the current picture in the blue ribbon division, Fury did not mince his words. "He does not. All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury sends immediate message to Anthony Joshua after forcing rival to quit
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury sends immediate message to Anthony Joshua after forcing rival to quit

The 'Gypsy King' was eager to fire a warning to his long-time rival just moments after stopping Mariusz Wach over in Thailand on Friday night

View Image Tyson Fury was quick to send a message to Anthony Joshua just moments after beating Mariusz Wach (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Tyson Fury is not convinced a fight with Anthony Joshua will materialise despite upholding his end of the bargain after forcing Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool.

‌



The former world champion ended a year-long hiatus back in April when he outpointed Russian powerhouse Arslanbek Makhmudov in front of over 60,000 fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Watching ringside was long-time rival Joshua - who refused to enter the ring and face off with Fury.

‌



Both men signed to fight each other just days later, but were first tasked with getting through respective tune-up fights. Joshua takes on Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night, while Fury returned on Friday evening against Wach. And despite eating a clubbing right hand in the second, the 'Gypsy King' controlled the contest before the Polish veteran eventually quit at the end of the seventh.

‌



And Fury was eager to tear into rival Joshua just moments after getting his hand raised. “I got through my test tonight. Let’s see if he gets through his test. The biggest test of it all is how big his balls are. I think he’s a big s***house. In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me. Let’s see if he ever does. I’m not convinced," he said.

There had been talk of Fury jetting straight from Thailand to Jeddah for tomorrow night's contest, but that will not be the case. The 37-year-old is due to fly back home to the Isle of Man, having been away from wife Paris and his children for over two months.

‌



“Will I balls. I’ll go and face off with my wife," he explained. “I’ve been away the last six or seven months. I’m definitely not going to Jeddah. I’m going home to my wife and kids who have been supporting me from a distance. I’ve been away in training camp for 10 weeks. Both men signed to fight each other - with the bout pencilled in for Wembley in November. But Saudi boxing chief Turki Al-Sheikh is insisting on a 4am start time in the UK in order to capture the American TV market.

And it seems as if even he does not have a clue after stating: “I’ll regroup, and hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we’re going to head. Who the f*** knows. Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!”

While Fury will not be ringside tomorrow, all eyes will still be on Joshua to get the job done on his return to the ring - seven months on from being involved in a tragic car crash just days after knocking out Jake Paul.

Sports.title: F1 star's dog caught weeing under Max Verstappen's number in Hungarian GP paddock
Sports.content:
F1 star's dog caught weeing under Max Verstappen's number in Hungarian GP paddock

Charles Leclerc couldn't stop laughing while his wife Alexandra was left mortified after their dog Leo was caught weeing up against the Red Bull garage in the Hungarian Grand Prix paddock

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc's dog Leo relieved himself on the wall of the Red Bull garage (Image: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Charles Leclerc was left in fits of laughter while his wife Alexandra looked utterly mortified as their beloved dog Leo chose a rather unfortunate moment to answer the call of nature during a stroll through the Hungarian Grand Prix paddock. Photographers at the Formula 1 event captured the hilarious scene as Leo Leclerc decided to relieve himself against the outside wall of the Red Bull garage.

‌



Snaps show the dog squatting to wee against the wall, directly beneath Max Verstappen's racing number three. Ferrari driver Leclerc saw the funny side, chuckling as he whipped out his own phone to photograph the moment, while his wife Alexandra, who had Leo's lead in hand, appeared utterly stunned and clasped her hand to her mouth.

‌



Unsurprisingly, it wasn't long before the images spread like wildfire across social media. "Pee one for Leo," quipped one amused fan, while many were quick to crown it the standout moment of the weekend, including one X user who wrote: "Leo really stole the spotlight in the paddock today."

‌



Even the official Red Bull account got in on the act. Responding to one post featuring a snap of the deed, the Red Bull account replied: "No Leo, that is so not right" - a nod to Toto Wolff's notorious radio message from the dramatic conclusion of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. They subsequently shared their own image of the scene, with a note pinned to the wall bearing the message: "Leo was here."

It followed the stewards convening in Budapest and concluding that Leclerc ought to have faced a penalty at the previous weekend's Belgian Grand Prix. He was briefly examined for making contact with Oscar Piastri early in the Spa-Francorchamps race, but they opted to take no further action against the Monegasque driver.

‌



View 2 Images Leclerc's wife Alexandra looked mortified as their dog Leo relieved itself on the Red Bull garage (Image: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Leclerc, who completed the race in second place, appeared uncomfortable afterwards as he viewed a replay of the incident in the cool down room while awaiting the podium ceremony, and subsequently conceded that he had escaped punishment. He said: "At the end of the day, my view in the car is that I try to push the things to the limit.

"I think with Oscar it was a bit on the other side, so that's probably not the way I want to race all the time. It's also risky for me at the end of the day. You're always trying to leave the smallest place available. That was maybe a bit too sketchy."

Article continues below

A discussion took place in Budapest before this weekend's racing, the first of two planned for this year where drivers meet with stewards to examine the application of regulations and propose possible amendments to the standards guidelines.

During that discussion, it is understood the stewards acknowledged that Leclerc should have received a penalty for his part in that specific collision.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury sets up Anthony Joshua fight as rival QUITS on his stool
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury sets up Anthony Joshua fight as rival QUITS on his stool

Tyson Fury took on Mariusz Wach on Friday, 24 hours before Anthony Joshua takes to the ring for his own warm-up clash ahead of the all-British heavyweight showdown

View 2 Images Tyson Fury beat Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand (Image: AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit)

Tyson Fury stopped Mariusz Wach to uphold his end of his bargain with Anthony Joshua.

‌



Fury was fighting for the second time this year having outpointed Arslanbek Makhmudov in London in April. He had insisted on a second warm-up bout before he takes on Joshua in November - and Fury made no mistake against 46-year-old Polish veteran Wach in Thailand on Friday.

‌



Fury now faces a nervous wait for Joshua to take to the ring in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night against Kristian Prenga. Victory for the Olympic champion should see a date and venue finally announced for the all-British heavyweight showdown.

‌



Fury, who was fighting in front of 1,500 fans and donating all ticket proceeds to a children's charity, began patiently, feinting with his jab before turning southpaw. He continued in that stance through the second round as Wach ate four jabs in succession before firing back with a right hand. Fury then landed a three-punch combination after the bell and was forced to apologise.

The 37-year-old continued to switch between stances in the third round as Wach began to tire. The Pole was content to lean on Fury having outweighed the Brit at Friday's weigh-in. But the 'Gypsy King' continued to jab his way through the fight while playing to the crowd in the fourth session.

‌



Wach reminded Fury he was still in the fight with a solid right hand in the fifth round. Fury responded by pinning the Pole in the corner and firing off his uppercut to leave Wach feeling the pace by the halfway mark. In the sixth, the onus was on the Morecambe brawler to up the tempo after chants of "there is only one Tyson Fury" echoed around the small arena.

A barrage of heavy punches from the Brit forced Wach to retreat to the corner, but a tired Wach continued to grapple and hold on for dear life. However, with the crowd heavily on Fury's side, he responded with some nice work on the inside with some clean and heavy shots.

‌



And after appearing leggy in the seventh round, Wach was checked over by the doctor and after a brief discussion with his team, the fight was waved off.

Reacting to the win post-fight, he said: “People say, ‘Why’s he fighting in here? He’s just had 12 rounds in April.’ Of course, I’m going to fight again. I’ve had one fight in two years. This is my second fight in two years. Of course, I wanted to get the rounds in. I want to be active.

“It’s not just the boxing in the ring. It’s spilt over the fight week, the press conference, the weigh-in, the nerves — everything."

‌



View 2 Images All eyes now turn to Joshua following Fury's dominant win over Wach (Image: AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit)

All eyes will now be on Joshua on Saturday night over in Jeddah when he takes on Prenga. Providing 'AJ' comes away unscathed, both Joshua and Fury will finally end their decade-long feud. Let’s see if he ever does. I’m not convinced." There had been talk that the former world champion would fly over to the Middle East to be ringside for his bitter rival's meeting with Prenga, but that won't be the case.

“Will I balls. I’ll go and face off with my wife," he joked. “I’ve been away the last six or seven months. I’m definitely not going to Jeddah. I’m going home to my wife and kids who have been supporting me from a distance. I’ve been away in training camp for 10 weeks. I was away before that for four months, so I’m going to go home and have a rest."

Sports.title: Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’
Sports.content:
Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’

Questions were asked about Egan’s position with Amo Racing after Rossa Ryan rode a double for the team in Ireland at the weekend

View 2 Images Kia Joorabchian: backed David Egan (Image: Tattersalls)

Kia Joorabchian has issued a vote of confidence in Amo Racing’s contracted jockey David Egan.

‌



Questions were raised about Egan’s position within the ambitious football agent’s team after he was not in the saddle when two horses ran at the Curragh last weekend. Rossa Ryan, Egan’s predecessor with Amo, rode instead and was successful on both Robson De Aguiar-trained runners, notably in the Group 2 Minstrel Stakes.

‌



Without immediate clarification from Amo, online bookmaker Betway offered odds of 4-1 about Frankie Dettori, who has been an ambassador for the team since retiring in February, riding for the owners in the UK before the end of 2027.

‌



Chelmsford racecourse saved after takeover with racing close to returning READ MORE :

While Dettori laughed off the suggestion, Egan said: “There’s been no quotes from anyone and I’d like to say no comment from me.

“I’ve got no comment on the situation. I’m declared to ride a horse on Friday for Amo, plan to ride for him on Saturday and even into next week so no comment.”

Egan and Joorabchian were together at Ascot where the Amo-owned, Charlie Fellowes-trained Treasurer finished seventh of ten in the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes.

‌



Before the race Joorabchian spoke for the first time about the situation to Sky Sports Racing.

View 2 Images David Egan: staying in Amo Racing job

He said: “Rossa Ryan still rides for me, Kevin Stott rode for me this year and David has been part of our team for two and a half years.

‌



“We treasure him very much. He’s a very, very important part of the team. Regardless of what people think of the operation and what he is, he means a lot to us.

“He’s been to America for us, he’s been all over the world for us and he will continue, hopefully, to have a very, very successful season for us. If people want to make stories about us because it suits them, that suits them.”

Asked why Ryan rode the horses in Ireland, he said: “Because that was outside the country. He had ridden all week, he had been very tired, I felt he was very tired. I felt he needed a small break and I think a break would have done him well. I wanted him to come back refreshed.

Article continues below

“Why? Because we have Goodwood, we have York, we have multiple races.”

He added: “Egan is my man, he’s always been my man. It doesn’t mean we don’t have a right to give someone a break or a rest for a day.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's private thoughts World Cup final players' behaviour revealed
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's private thoughts World Cup final players' behaviour revealed

Gianni Infantino praised Spain's players for their exemplary conduct - a stark contrast to Argentina's behaviour after their World Cup 1-0 defeat

View Image Luis de la Fuente has revealed Gianni Infantino's praise for Spain's players (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has declared Spain a shining example to football, making the statement in the wake of the World Cup final's shocking scenes of violence triggered by Argentina's players. Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the brawl, throwing punches and kicks at rival players as they celebrated the 1-0 triumph in New Jersey

‌



An extra‑time winner from Ferran Torres sealed the win for La Roja, who lifted the iconic trophy. Argentina were already down to ten men after Enzo Fernandez was sent off for a reckless moment late in normal time. Tensions then exploded after the final whistle, with violence breaking out across the MetLife Stadium pitch.

‌



Others were dragged into the chaos as the situation descended into mayhem, though calm was eventually restored before the medal ceremony and Spain hoisted the trophy. FIFA have subsequently launched an investigation into the distasteful scenes.

‌



Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes speaks out on Argentina World Cup conspiracy theories after sparking Spain brawl READ MORE :

Infantino had previously met Spain boss Luis de la Fuente at the Olympic Games, where the Spain boss later disclosed the details of their discussion. Those views were repeated after the World Cup, with Infantino emphasising that his admiration for Spain's players remains valid today.

"I always say that private conversations should be private, but in this case, I think it's worth mentioning," he told Marca. "Why? Because it highlights the caliber of our players. Look, Infantino and I met at the Olympic Games, where we won the silver medal. The players' behaviour was spectacular.

"They put on their medals, they didn't take them off, they enjoyed the closing ceremony. When the ceremony was over, Infantino came up to me and said, 'Mister, your players are an example.'".

‌



"And many of those players were in this final. He reminded me of it the other day, saying, 'What I told you at the Olympic Games still applies today. What an example of everything: team spirit, camaraderie, generosity, sacrifice, and footballing greatness.' And that's something to be proud of. It's the greatest source of pride, beyond anything purely related to football."

This stands in sharp contrast to the conduct of certain Argentina players following the final whistle in the World Cup final - not only igniting confrontations on the pitch, but with multiple squad members also turning their backs as Spain received the trophy.

It's a moment that couldn't be further removed from the professionalism and dignity Infantino recognised in his exchange with De La Fuente, commending Spain's players for their collective spirit, humility and behaviour throughout both competitions.

‌

Whether the animosity between Spain and Argentina will carry over into the competition remains unclear, though it will mark the next chance for both sides to add silverware to their collections.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
