World.title: Wildfires near Boston Bar, B.C., merge as district says some residents still refusing to evacuate
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Two of the three out-of-control wildfires threatening Boston Bar, B.C., and surrounding communities have merged.

In a Thursday night update, the B.C. Wildfire Service said the Anderson Creek fire, which broke out Tuesday, had grown to merge with the southern edge of the massive Ainslie Creek fire.

The two covered an area of more than 264.1 square kilometres as of Friday morning.

“This really has not changed our response, it just means they’ve merged together into one incident," B.C. Wildfire Service fire information officer Jean Strong said.

The Brunswick Creek wildfire also continues to burn out of control, at 72 square kilometres, on the other side of the Fraser River, leaving the community essentially encircled by fires.

Together, the trio make up the Brunswick wildfire complex.

The Brunswick Creek wildfire is seen burning near Boston Bar, B.C., on July 6. (B.C. Wildfire Service)

Highway 1 remains closed between Spuzzum Creek Road and the Jackass Summit, and more than 450 properties in the area are under evacuation orders.

The Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD), however, said some residents have refused to leave.

"We understand evacuation reluctance, however, these individuals are violating the law. This action leaves them at risk," the district said in a statement.

"With the rapidly changing weather and wildfire behaviour, it significantly increases the risk of not knowing, before it is too late to leave the area, or before exit access is cut off. Leaving the area is for their protection and the protection of first responders."

Boston Bar evacuee Kyle Wood said he saw the Anderson Creek wildfire grow rapidly on Tuesday. (CBC News)

Boston Bar evacuee Kyle Wood watched how quickly the Anderson Creek wildfire grew on Tuesday.

“The trees were candling right beside the road," he said.

“By the time I got to my dad’s, I just looked over and half the mountain was on fire," he added.

“So we went back to my place, packed up and got out. And by the time we got out we could see the red of the flames coming up over the hill closer to Boston Bar."

The B.C. Wildfire Service said its number one priority in the area remains protecting the community, and that crews are on the ground "actively defending structures around Boston Bar, the Boston Bar First Nation and Canyon Alpine."

Personnel are on the ground patrolling for hotspots and maintaining sprinkler systems, the service said.

More than 100 active wildfires across B.C.

The fires around Boston Bar are among 103 burning across British Columbia on Friday, more than half of them out of control.

Most of the fires are burning in the southern half of the province.

“The Cariboo Fire Centre has seen a lot of activity in the last 24 hours and we expect that will continue. There are wildfires in the areas near Williams Lake and Clinton we’re continuing to respond to," Smart said.

“We expect we will continue to see that aggressive fire behaviour in the coming days, as we continue to see that hot, dry weather continue, we’ll keep seeing those gusty winds."

The wildfire service said the Fiftynine Creek wildfire northwest of Clinton has grown to more than 167 square kilometres, triggering an evacuation order and alerts.

Overnight, the Thompson-Nicola Regional District expanded an evacuation order south of Clinton, due to the Pear Lake fire.

“We expect we will cibntnue ot see that aggressive fire behavour in the coming days, as we continue to see that hot, dry weather continue, we’ll keep seeing those gusty winds.

The Fiftynine Creek fire is seen burning on July 21. (B.C. Wildfire Service)

On Thursday, TNRD community and emergency services manager Kevin Skrepnek confirmed that structures on about 20 properties in the region were "impacted" by the fires, with the damage ranging from melted siding to a complete burn-down.

In B.C.'s southeast, the entire city of Kimberley remains under an evacuation alert due to the nearby Bootleg complex of wildfires, including a cluster of wildfires burning west of the city.

Hugh Murdoch, incident commander on the complex, said there are seven fires that firefighters are closely watching in the region, and he is happy to share that the fire behaviour "has been held in check for the most part."

But Murdoch said the weather forecast was "far from favourable," with "no rain in sight" and above-seasonal temperatures expected for the foreseeable future.

B.C. Hydro said Friday that some customers were experiencing flickering lights as a result of wildfire activity.

"This is a result of smoke and ash from wildfires in the BC Southern Interior in proximity to our powerlines resulting in short and temporary interruptions in the flow of electricity on the impacted powerline," spokesperson Susie Rieder said in an email.

Rieder said the grid was performing as expected under challenging conditions, and that the system was capable of self correcting after a fault due to branches on power lines, lightning strikes or smoke or debris.

Scientists say human-caused climate change plays a key role in the province's worsening wildfire seasons, as B.C. grapples with drought, drier forests and more days with hotter temperatures.

World.title: Doctors are using a regulatory gap to prescribe an unauthorized peptide
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Despite Health Canada's warnings against the use of unauthorized peptides as a health and fitness shortcut, a CBC News investigation uncovered doctors using a regulatory loophole to prescribe one of the unproven products to patients.

The popularity of peptides has surged as fitness influencers endorse them to build muscle, reverse the signs of aging and lose weight.

Peptides are short amino acid chains naturally produced by the body that act as building blocks of larger proteins that support growth, metabolism and healing.

But unlike approved peptides used in medicine, such as insulin and GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic, Health Canada tells CBC "unauthorized peptide products sold for wellness purposes have not been assessed for safety, quality, or effectiveness."

And yet, CBC News found doctors promoting and prescribing a popular unauthorized peptide called Body Protection Compound-157 (BPC-157) that is touted to help accelerate muscle growth and tissue repair.

That's because the same regulator prohibiting BPC-157’s sale as an injectable drug or a licensed natural health product says it can be compounded as a pill by pharmacies — with a doctor's prescription.

"It's maddening," said Timothy Caulfield, a professor in the faculty of law and the school of public health and research director of the Health Law Institute at the University of Alberta.

Doctors should be "warning their patients about these products, not providing them," he said.

Hidden camera claims

CBC News journalists armed with hidden cameras visited two doctors — at clinics in Ontario and B.C. — that advertised unauthorized peptides to hear the health claims offered to patients.

"I'm on some peptides myself," said Dr. Shawn Seit, speaking to an undercover CBC journalist at his Rejuuv Medi Spa in Markham, Ont. "So, that's how safe I feel they are."

In a recorded one-on-one consultation, Seit said that BPC-157 "really helps in terms of healing and inflammation."

WATCH | Getting peptides through a loophole: How Canadians are getting unauthorized peptides | Duration 10:00 A CBC News hidden-camera investigation uncovers unauthorized peptides, such as BPC-157, being promoted across Canada. For The National, CBC’s Idil Mussa breaks down what the team uncovered and how the findings sparked a series of new investigations by Health Canada.

In B.C., Dr. Charles Jiang claimed, until recently, on his Richmond Anti-Aging Clinic website that BPC-157 can be used for "musculoskeletal and gut lining repair." He also told a CBC journalist during an in-person visit that unlike peptides sold online, the ones he prescribes are safe.

"When you order online, you never know what is the truth behind it," said Jiang. "If you come to us we are professional doctors."

Caulfield says physicians that prescribe unauthorized peptides are capitalizing on a fad that could be risky.

They're "leveraging a longevity wellness trend," he said. "Despite the fact there's no evidence and real potential harm."

Jiang did not respond to CBC's repeated requests for comment.

In emailed statements, Seit said his aim is "always directed at optimizing my patients' care and treatment” and that he is permitted to compound BPC-157 as a natural health product (NHP), which Health Canada confirmed. The same is true of any doctor in the country.

Timothy Caulfield, a professor in the faculty of law and the school of public health and research director of the Health Law Institute at the University of Alberta, says doctors should be warning their patients about these products. (Curtis Trent)

Compounding BPC-157: A regulatory loophole

In a statement, Health Canada said "BPC‑157 has not been authorized, its safety, efficacy, and quality have not been assessed … and there is limited scientific evidence to support its use, including a lack of established human dosing protocols."

In addition, the regulator says BPC-157 is not approved for use in any NHPs in any form, including oral and injectable, but it can still be compounded for topical use or oral administration as an NHP.

That means doctors can prescribe BPC-157 to patients and compounding pharmacies — that mix custom medications — can formulate them.

"Nobody's minding the store," said Stuart Phillips, a professor of kinesiology at McMaster University in Hamilton.

"Health Canada won't approve it as a drug, but it slips through as a compounded natural health product, where the federal safety check basically doesn't happen."

Health Canada considers NHP compounding within a practitioner-patient relationship distinct from manufacturing and not subject to the same regulatory oversight.

"The practitioner-patient relationship is supposed to be where evidence gets turned into advice. But you can't practise evidence-based medicine on a substance that has no evidence," said Phillips.

The federal agency says compounding must not be used to circumvent the federal drug review and approval process, but Caulfield says that appears to be the case.

Stuart Phillips, a kinesiology professor at McMaster University, says when it comes to unauthorized peptides, there should be greater regulation and oversight. (Ousama Farag/CBC)

"BPC-157 is not an NHP," he said.

"Compounding is not meant to be a strategy that allows consumers to go around regulatory oversight, which seems to be what is happening here if they allow the application of NHP rules."



Seit said the prescriptions he provides "do not circumvent regulatory oversight." The regulatory bodies to which Jiang, Seit and those pharmacies belong had various responses.

In a statement to CBC News, the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario said the information physicians provide to patients or the public about treatments should be accurate and informed by evidence.

The College of Physicians and Surgeons of British Columbia said it doesn't have specific guidance on prescribing oral BPC-157, but expects "licensees to exercise professional judgment to ensure they are providing safe and appropriate patient care."

The Ontario College of Pharmacists says compounding an NHP using ingredients unauthorized by Health Canada could be investigated as a breach of professional conduct.

The College of Pharmacists of British Columbia states it "cannot be determined in general terms" whether a pharmacy has violated its standards.

Health Canada says it is illegal to promote health products that have not been authorized for sale, including compounded products tailored to individual patients.

After CBC News asked the department about the websites advertising BPC-157, it said it was investigating whether those activities complied with the Food and Drugs Act.

The mention of peptide therapy and BPC-157 was also taken down on Seit's and Jiang's websites after CBC News contacted them for comment.

All hype, no research

During CBC's undercover consultation, Seit admitted there was a lack of clinical human studies on BPC-157.

"A lot of these studies are based on animal models," he said. "They're not based on human models."

In an email to CBC News, he stated he was candid with his patients about the current research regarding BPC-157.

Jiang's clinic website also stated that BPC-157 had "limited human trial data."

Phillips, at McMaster University, says the lack of human trials raises serious questions about BPC-157's potential health risks.

"There are basically no published human efficacy trials for BPC-157."

Phillips says all he can find is one small safety study from a decade ago, and a trial that only started enrolling participants this past February.

Patricia Brubaker’s work helped pave the way for approved peptide medications like Ozempic. (Ousama Farag/CBC)

"Almost everything else is rodent work."

Patricia Brubaker, a professor emeritus of physiology at the University of Toronto, has taken a hard look at the research and has come to a similar conclusion about BPC-157's alleged benefits.

"Animal models do not always translate into humans. Dosing doesn't translate into humans. Safety doesn't translate into humans necessarily," said Brubaker.

Brubaker says drugs need to be carefully tested in stages before they are approved for use in people.

"It's really important that scientific discoveries are translated from the bench cells, animals into humans through a series of clinical trials that prove at every step, with increasing numbers of subjects, that this product is effective, that it's safe, and that you know how much of it to administer."

World.title: Heated Rivalry thirst traps: The Canadian export that won't quit
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

First it was Hudson Williams for Peloton.

Now it's François Arnaud for Under Armour.

It seems U.S. fitness brands can't get enough of the Canadian actors who portray the beloved fictional hockey players in Heated Rivalry ... and the internet is eating it up.

Both campaigns bear certain hallmarks that push them from equipment and sportswear  into clear thirst-trap territory: close-ups on chiselled abs, artistic beads of sweat and coquettish looks into the camera.

Everyone involved understands two things: Sex sells, and these particular stars are used to being objectified by men and women of all ages, in countries around the world.

Part ad, part advocacy

François Arnaud is openly bisexual, and the Under Armour  alludes to that by depicting both a man and a woman growing increasingly agitated as they not-so-subtly watch him work out.

"The ad is bisexual," said Joe Recupero, an associate professor of sports media at Toronto Metropolitan University. "I thought this is a really cool ad because when do you ever see ads directed at the bisexual community?"

He also commended Under Armour for releasing the ad after Pride month, at the risk of perhaps turning off some of its target demographic.

"It's very cheeky ... because it's subtle, but it's not so subtle."

Arnaud came out as bisexual in a social media post in September 2020, just before Bi Visibility Day. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

Under Armour is also clear about wanting Arnaud not just for his talent and looks but for what his Heated Rivalry character represents.

"The character he portrays ultimately finds his greatest success when he stops trying to fit someone else's mould and embraces who he truly is. That's a lesson that resonates deeply with us," Matt Dornic, the company's chief communications officer, said in a statement.

Peloton's message was more focused on self-love when it launched the Hudson Williams campaign in April.

"Our goal with this campaign was to capture that feeling of total freedom," chief marketing officer Megan Imbres said in a news release.

Captivated audience

The Peloton campaign — which featured Williams half-dancing and half-walking on a treadmill, lifting weights and working out with a trainer — quickly went viral. Heated Rivalry superfans made pilgrimages to downtown Toronto to see the ad on the big screen over Sankofa Square.

Arnaud's Under Armour ad is receiving a similarly enthusiastic response, garnering nearly 75,000 likes on its Instagram post during its first day online.

" Finally, the bisexual deities have answered our prayers," said one top commenter. "Oh, I love the way he holds up our flag," said another.

One self-declared bookstagrammer said, "I would like to personally thank all the marketing teams across the country."

Overexposure?

It has been eight months since Heated Rivalry premiered on Crave, and the stars of the show are still a favourite subject of gossip blogs, fan accounts and traditional media stories.

Season 2 isn't scheduled to air until April 2027. Until then, the most devoted fans are "reheating" or rewatching the series multiple times.

WATCH | Heated Rivalry's creator says show is about celebration: Why Heated Rivalry is hopecore coded | Duration 1:42 Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney tells The National's Ian Hanomansing he wanted the show to be a celebration of queer joy when audiences are more used to seeing punishment in storylines involving queer love and sex.

But Recupero said he doesn't think the public is anywhere close to reaching Heated Rivalry fatigue.

"I keep waiting for the bottom to drop out and the fandom to cool down and for oversaturation," he said. "I think this is going to be something people are really looking at and studying about when is the oversaturation point? And I don't believe we've hit it yet."

World.title: 2 cyclists crossing Canada for men's mental health have bikes stolen in downtown Winnipeg
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Two men on a charity ride to raise awareness for men's mental health had their bikes stolen in downtown Winnipeg on Friday morning.

Val Duquenne, 24, and Thomas Clark, 23, stopped in for an interview at CBC Manitoba's Portage Avenue studio.

When they left, their bikes were gone. The U-lock securing the bikes to a rack on the back of their car, parked on Young Street just off Portage, had been cut off.

"We were in there maybe 30, 40 minutes max," Clark said after returning to CBC from making a police report. "My jaw dropped, and I started running towards the car, looking around. It's disappointing."

The thief, or thieves, left an old bike behind while riding off with the two stolen bikes.

" We didn’t know Winnipeg was this low. We haven’t had a single issue in any major city," they posted on their Instagram page.

"Those bikes were given to us by the community. Mine was given to me by a veteran … so it's definitely hard," Duquenne said.

"We've been working really hard for this. It's been non-stop since we started planning this two months ago."

The friends, from New Brunswick, started their Men Don't Ride Alone trek in North Sydney, N.S., on June 22, with the goal of reaching Victoria in September. They've raised $6,500 so far for Movember Canada, with a goal of raising $250,000.

Duquenne and Clark have made police reports and posted about the incident on their social media pages, hoping the bikes are found.

Otherwise, they're going to have to start raising money for new ones.

"They were expensive bikes, probably [worth] $15,000 together. So it's definitely a big hit to take," Duquenne said.

Cross-country rides halted by thefts

Over the past decade, at least five cyclists crossing the country have had their rides cut short in Winnipeg due to their bikes being stolen.

"Unfortunately bike theft continues to be a property crime of opportunity that challenges our community and law enforcement," Winnipeg police said in an email statement to CBC News, urging people to use Project 529 to register bikes.

Duquenne's bike is a Trek SL 5 with a blue and black frame, and the brand name in white along the down tube.

Clark's bike is a Cannondale Synapse, all black, with "Cannondale" in white lettering on the top frame.

Anyone with information is asked to call the property crime unit 204-986-2426. Anonymous tips can be called in to 204-786-8477 or submitted online.

Duquenne's bike is seen at top, with Clark's at bottom. (mendontridealone/Instagram)

The impetus behind the ride was Duquenne's struggles with mental health and substance abuse, which led to him admitting himself to hospital in Moncton, N.B., last September.

"When I got out and I got help, I wanted to make a difference in the world and I thought of this way, and Thomas was right along with me the whole time," he said during Friday morning's interview with CBC Manitoba's Information Radio.

"It was really good to get help. And that's the big point of our mission, is to let people know that they can seek help and that life does get better at the end of the day."

The men have been taking turns doing the ride. While one pedals, the other follows along in a car.

The car is clearly marked with the cause the men are promoting, which makes Friday's theft that much more sad, said Clark.

"Whoever did take them … just didn't care."

Other than Friday's disheartening incident, the experience has been rewarding, Clark said.

"I's been an incredible journey so far. It really has. It's really cool being able to see the country at about 20 km/h. We've seen a lot of cool things and met a lot of cool people."

Thomas Clark, left, and Val Duquenne say they will finish their journey one way or another. (Fernand Detillieux/Radio-Canada)

He was diagnosed with ADHD when he was a young boy, and says there are a lot of mental struggles that come with having a condition that makes it hard to pay attention and sit still.

"So when [Duquenne] came to me with this [idea], I thought, hey, this connects right with what I believe in," Clark said.

Along with rides, rests and interviews, the men have also been documenting the journey on social media.

"[It’s] only us two doing everything. So it's been really hard to keep up with," said Duquenne.

The men say some donations have already come in since they posted about the incident on social media, and they plan to visit bike shops in Winnipeg to see what they might be able to afford.

One way or another, they plan to complete their journey.

"If we have to run it, we'll run it. We're making it happen," Duquenne said.

"We will finish this and keep the cause going, for sure," added Clark.

World.title: LeBron James heading to 76ers, saying it will be his 'last decision'
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

LeBron James is heading to the Philadelphia 76ers.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer made the announcement on social media Friday, saying it will be his "last decision" and that it comes after he strongly considered retirement.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time," James said.

A four-time NBA champion, James wrote he was "done" when his 23rd NBA season ended and that it was his last with the Los Angeles Lakers.

"I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game," James wrote. "I still truly love this game, and I have more to give."

The 41-year-old James is set to sign a modest two-year contract worth $8 million US with the Sixers, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

"I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family," James wrote. "What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning."

Fanatics already had his No. 23 jersey on sale for $125 with delivery not expected until the end of August.

Much as James did for Cleveland when he ended a 56-year championship drought for the city by leading the Cavaliers to the title in 2016, he can snap a lengthy title drought for the Sixers.

The Sixers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round by the NBA champion New York Knicks.

All-star lineup

James joins a 76ers team that has not won an NBA championship since 1983 and has not advanced out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs since 2001.

The 76ers should boast one of the top starting fives in the NBA with fellow all-stars Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, the 2024 NBA Finals MVP, a five-time all-star and the league's fourth-leading scorer this past season acquired in a stunning offseason deal with the Celtics.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro even proclaimed Friday as LeBron James Day in the state.

Turned out, new 76ers team president Mike Gansey was just getting started with his summer of surprises.

No move, of course, hits like James's arrival.

He won his four NBA championships in stops with Cleveland, Miami and the Los Angeles Lakers. James left the Lakers after an eight-season run highlighted by the 2020 NBA title.

James is the NBA's oldest active player at 41 and the only player in league history to have a career spanning 23 seasons; this coming season will be his 24th. Speculation has been rampant for more than two months about his future, officially starting in May when the Lakers were eliminated from the NBA playoffs.

James's resume is beyond compare in NBA history. He's a 22-time all-star, a 21-time All-NBA selection, a four-time most valuable player, a four-time NBA Finals MVP, a three-time all-star game MVP, and was a member of the NBA's 75th anniversary team.

He's also coming off a season where he averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists per game. For his career, he's averaged 26.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 7.4 assists in more than 1,600 games.

James started his career in Cleveland in 2003 and spent seven seasons with the Cavaliers before heading to Miami for four seasons where he won his first two NBA titles. He then returned to Cleveland for four more seasons, including that title run in 2016, and left in 2018 for the Lakers.

Cleveland and Miami were believed to be on James's radar again as he weighed this decision.

"Thank you LA. Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!" James wrote.

For the next two seasons, James's professional home is in Philadelphia.

World.title: Bystanders help rescue passengers from seaplane crash near B.C.-Wash. border
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A seaplane crashed and later caught fire while making an emergency landing on the shoreline of Sucia Island near the B.C.-Washington border on Thursday evening, according to U.S. officials, drawing emergency teams from both countries.

By the time first responders arrived, several recreational boaters who saw the Kenmore Air plane go down had rescued the plane's pilot and 10 passengers from the wreckage, according to Nathan Butler, a member of the command staff for San Juan Island EMS.

"Before we ever got to the scene, they got all of the patients on their boats, they tied [three boats] together ... and they had blankets and used first aid to bandage people's head injuries," he said.

He added that two of the boaters were an off-duty medic and trauma nurse.

"They honestly did an amazing job and made that situation much better than it would have been.... They truly were heroes last night."

Everyone on the plane was transported to nearby hospitals by boat and air lift, Butler said.

The San Juan County Sheriff's office posted on Facebook that passengers' injuries ranged from broken bones and lacerations to head injuries. The post said one patient was in critical condition, but no deaths had been reported.

In a statement, Kenmore Air said the de Havilland DHC-3 Otter aircraft departed from Lake Union, Seattle, before it was "involved in an accident" at about 5:15 p.m. PT Thursday.

"We are grateful that everyone aboard has been accounted for, and our immediate focus is ensuring our passengers and pilot receive the care and support they need," said CEO David Gudgel in the statement.

The company cancelled all scheduled flights for Friday, and said it would not speculate on the cause of the accident.

The U.S. Coast Guard said the cause of the emergency landing and fire are under investigation.

The Canadian Coast Guard ship Siyay and B.C. Air Ambulance, operated by B.C. Emergency Health Services, responded to the incident, in addition to a number of U.S. Coast Guard and Washington state agencies, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.

BCEHS said three air ambulances and critical care crew were "staged but later stood down as they were not required in the response."

A file photo of a Kenmore Air plane on the ocean. (Kenmore Air/Facebook)

Investigation still underway

Mike Hairston, undersheriff for the San Juan County Sheriff's office, said within about 30 minutes of receiving reports of the crash, he and other dispatch crew from the command team on Orcas Island had deployed American and Canadian emergency teams to the scene.

He said he was relieved everyone on board the plane had survived.

"I mean, anytime we have a plane go down, there's always that chance — plus this happened on a remote island that is only accessible by a helicopter or a boat."

On Friday morning, he and staff from the Department of Fish and Wildlife headed to the crash site to review the scene and take photos of the plane on the shoreline at low tide.

World.title: Book Review: The Instrument Must Not Matter makes its own kind of music
World.content:
Article content

Never off-putting or pretentious — a testy, all-too human protagonist like Lila helps offset that possibility — Fischer Guy skilfully manoeuvres a tightrope tethered between the inner life of the artist and the oblivious exterior world in which artistic and intellectual freedoms are imperilled by those for whom ignorance is its own primitive art form. The loss of individual choice is a sort of death for artists and art and a warning to everyone else. The ballet slipper crushed under the heel of the jackboot represents the end of personhood, the sublimation of all that makes us who and what we are, whether we are rehearsing arias or trimming trees.

World.title: Colombia’s “Shield of the Americas” to operate from Medellin: De la Espriella
World.content:
Medellin will be the home of the US-led “Shield of the Americas” security program, according to Colombia’s President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella and Mayor Federico Gutierrez.

At a meeting with authorities from the Antioquia province, De la Espriella and Gutierrez agreed that Colombia’s second largest city is the “head of the snake of drug trafficking and organized crime.”

From Medellin, the metropolitan area, most orders are sent out to the rest of the country. So we’re going to focus our efforts on Medellin to fight crime. Abelardo de la Espriella

The announcement followed alleged calls between De la Espriella, US President Donald Trump and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and meetings between incoming Defense Minister Jorge Mora and the US’ Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for the Americas, Joseph Humire.

Following the meeting, Mora and Humire announced “Plan Patriota 2.0” and the creation of a “Regional Training Center against Drug Trafficking and Transnational Threats,” which would be “aimed at improving interoperability, operational readiness, and cooperation with allied countries” from the Americas.

During these meetings, the parties explored the joint development of a new bilateral program for cooperation and strategic assistance with a regional scope, known as Plan Patriota 2.0. This initiative is conceived as part of Colombia’s accession to the American Coalition Against the Cartels and is based on the design of the new Policy on Defense, Security, and Civic Coexistence, as well as on the strategy for military and police campaigns in priority areas for the restoration and stabilization of security. Jorge Mora

Plan Patriota was a US-backed military strategy that was implemented by former President Alvaro Uribe between 2003 and 2006.

The plan sought to dismantle the military organization of the now-defunct FARC guerrilla group, which it largely did while also killing thousands and forcibly displacing hundreds of thousands civilians.

De la Espriella has said that he seeks to restart Plan Colombia and seek to militarily destroy groups that were formed during and after peace processes with the FARC and the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

World.title: “Water will run out:” Colombia declares emergency over upcoming El Niño
World.content:
Colombia’s government agreed to declare a national emergency over the consequences of El Niño, a climate phenomenon that is expected to bring extreme drought in December.

According to the government’s environmental institute, IDEAM, this year’s Niño could become the worst since the 1950’s and will peak between November 2026 an March 2027.

During a minister’s council, President Gustavo Petro said that excessive heat and water shortages could lead to energy shortages in regions that rely on hydroelectric dams for their electricity.

Petro asked Finance Minister German Avila to transfer COP4 trillion ($1.2 billion) to disaster management agency UNGRD to double the purchase of solar panels to lessen the demand on these hydroelectric dams.

In December last year, the UNGRD already signed a COP4.2 trillion deal with electricity firm Gecelca to buy solar panels.

In order to maintain food production, the president ordered the purchase of desalination plants for the Caribbean region.

Water is what’s going to run out—we don’t know to what extent, but hopefully Bogotá won’t have to suffer through this again. So, any drinking water supply project that’s already been designed but lacks funding must be funded. Drinking water—all the desalination plants we can bring in, because we don’t build them in Colombia — in all the towns in the northern Caribbean. President Gustavo Petro

Last but not least, Petro urged the Justice Ministry to secure “the accelerated surrender of lands, 500 thousand hectares, that have not been awarded” to landless farmers.

“Provide more land and more water to grow food, grow more food in Colombia, because the sun is going to scorch a lot of food and burn crops. And so it’s likely that we’ll be able to make up for the loss in food supply over these six months with new food supplies,” said the president.

Petro urged his ministers to be careful of corruption, which sank the UNGRD in a crisis in early 2024 and resulted in the detentions of multiple government officials.

World.title: De la Espriella denied aspired control over Colombia’s Congress
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress denied control over the legislative agenda to President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella and voted for a president loyal to former President Alvaro Uribe.

De la Espriella proposed his friend, Senator Alfredo Deluque of the U Party, to assume the leadership of the Senate, which would have given the government control over the congressional agenda.

Ahead of the vote, eight parties expressed their support for Deluque’s candidacy, which would have given him a 55-vote majority in the anonymous vote.

Former President Alvaro Uribe, whose Democratic Center party would be granted the presidency, accused “Abelardo’s circle” of trying to “get rid of this party” and vowed to “defend ourselves.”

Uribe had put up Democratic Center Senator Honorio Henriquez for the job and ordered his 17 senators to stick to their original vote.

If the Tiger roars to destroy the Democratic Center, we’ll have to become hardworking bees and defend ourselves, just like bees do when they’re attacked… I’m frightened by the idea circulating among De La Espriella’s inner circle of destroying that party. Former President Alvaro Uribe

The former president got the support of President Gustavo Petro, arguably Abelardo’s biggest political enemy.

At a rally that was held ahead of the vote, Petro warned senators of his leftist Historic Pact party “not to vote for fascism.”

Under the leadership of Senate bench leader Ivan Cepeda, who lost the presidential election to De la Espriella last month, all 26 of the pact’s senators voted for Henriquez.

Enjoying the secrecy of their vote, dissidents from the parties who were ordered to vote Deluque also turned on the president-elect and delivered Henrique 56 votes. Deluque ended up with only 45.

Less than three weeks before taking office, De la Espriella lost the loyalty of its largest coalition partner in Congress and will have to negotiate his agenda with them.

World.title: Petro calls for “peaceful resistance” against Colombia’s incoming “viceroyalty”
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro called on the people to “prepare peaceful resistance” to the “viceroyalty” that “has been imposed as the president of Colombia.”

During an Independence Day speech in the poor south of Bogota, Petro told thousands of supporters that “the next president of Colombia will be a servant to the rulers of the United States who helped him ‘get elected’.”

“We move from the status of a republic to the status of a viceroyalty again, just like 216 years ago,” said Petro, who on Sunday accepted to become the political leader of the leftist opposition.

It is time to give the second cry of independence… Shout freedom and resistance! Gustavo Petro

Rather than a repetition of the 1810 revolution, the outgoing president proposed to “prepare for peaceful resistance” in defense of communities who benefited from the government’s reforms.

How do you repeal the decree on hourly work that ends the labor reform that created stability, a vital wage, and better working conditions? How? Well, with a permanent general strike of millions of working men and women in Colombia! It is not just by shouting, it is not just by raising flags, they are already used to that… No, it is with a production strike, which is permitted by the National Constitution of Colombia, it is a universal right! And that indeed is civil disobedience! If they are going to strike down the stabilities, the working conditions achieved in this government, a general and indefinite strike in Colombia! Gustavo Petro

Petro threatened to “surround the centers of illegitimate power in Colombia until legitimacy exists once again, which can only be achieved through free popular decision without algorithms, and without foreign money.”

To protect the people, the president suggested the creation of unarmed “liberatory guards” that work in a network, “because they want to kill.”

Wherever they touch a neighborhood, wherever they touch a peasant estate, the network must summon solidarity, it must become a demonstration of all adjacent neighborhoods, of all adjacent villages, of the whole country if necessary. Gustavo Petro

“The only way to stop fascism,” said Petro, “is in peace. It is with joy, but it is with millions and millions of Colombian men and women.”

World.title: Petro to assume political leadership of Colombia’s leading leftist party
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro said Sunday that he would become the leader of Colombia’s largest political party on the left, the Historic Pact.

In a tweet, Petro responded to Senator Ivan Cepeda, who proposed him as party president at a political rally in the city of Tunja on Saturday.

Petro said he would “accept the proposal of my party after surrendering power to the far-right President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

The president said he would first go “on a vacation I deserve and didn’t have during four years of governance.”

We will work toward peace and social justice and for a national agreement that prevents violent confrontation among Colombians, and we will seek to contribute to the democratic stability of the countries that Simon Bolívar liberated. President Gustavo Petro

The Historic Pact party was formed in March from a coalition of multiple parties that have long supported the political careers of Petro and Cepeda.

Following a significant electoral victory, the party became the largest of Colombia and will assume 25 of 103 seats in the Senate.

Petro’s former party, Colombia Humana, contributed 12 senators to the collective.

The president started his political career while being a member of the M-19 guerrilla group, which demobilized in 1990.

Petro was elected to the House of Representatives in 1998 an became a senator in 2006.

Between 2012 and 2015, the president was mayor of the capital Bogota.

Petro has been the most popular and powerful leftist politician since the violent death of Liberal Party leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan in 1948, and was sanctioned by the US Government amid his opposition to the genocide in Gaza.

The president has insisted that his successor won the June elections through fraud and has refused to recognize De la Espriella as his successor.

World.title: Colombia’s peace and human rights offices to close: De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella announced on Monday that he will close the Peace Commissioner’s Office, which was in charge of negotiating peace and implementing peace deals with illegal armed groups.

“The Office of the Peace Commissioner is coming to an end, because there will be no more sham peace processes during my administration,” said De la Espriella in his weekly address to the nation that was broadcast on his social media platforms.

According to the far-right president-elect, who will take office on August 7, other presidential commissioners that will disappear are those of National Reconciliation. and the Office of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law.

The functions of these offices will be taken over by the Interior, Foreign and Defense ministries that, according to De la Espriella, have been doubling the work of the presidential commissioners.

“These are functions that, by law, are already carried out by other ministries,” so the government can “avoid duplication and extra costs,” said the president-elect.

De la Espriella seems keen to abruptly end the peace policy of his predecessor, President Gustavo Petro, for being too lenient to illegal armed groups.

The president-elect also promised to close war crimes tribunal JEP, which has been trying thousands of former guerrillas and former members of the military.

De la Espriella could only do this through legislation that would change the constitution and the international treaties that protect the victims of an armed conflict between the State and the now-defunct guerrilla organization FARC.

World.title: Petro to seek court order to annul election of De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro said Tuesday that he will seek a court order to annul the election of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a post on social media platform X, Petro said he had gather enough evidence to prove that his successor “was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes.”

“Today we are presenting the body of evidence we have gathered to the representatives elected by the people, and we will file a lawsuit with the courts to annul the elections, as is our duty,” said the outgoing president.

We are not making things up when we say that Abelardo’s government was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes included in the percentage automatically adjusted by algorithms created by private Israeli companies with the endorsement of their genocidal government. President Gustavo Petro

“We are facing not only the imminent rise of fascism in Colombia but also what may be the greatest threat to global democracy since Hitler’s time,” said Petro.

In a response that was broadcast on his social media channels, De la Espriella reiterated that Petro was a “tyrant” who was trying to perpetuate power through a coup d’etat with the help of the leftist runner-up in the election, Senator Ivan Cepeda.

Even before becoming a candidate, I warned you: Petro is a tyrant in the making who seeks to perpetuate himself in power by any means necessary. And today, as the president-elect of all of you, I ratify what I have said for so many years. This is no longer an analysis or an opinion; it is a palpable reality. From the moment nearly 13 million Colombians stood by me to defeat him and his political frontman, Petro and Cepeda began their Plan B to stay in power, no matter what it takes. And they want to do so through a coup d’état. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

The president-elect asked the armed forces “to protect the Constitution and democracy, and to disobey any order that Petro may be giving to the contrary.”

Resistance, dear compatriots. We cannot allow them to snatch away what we achieved at the ballot box in an epic democratic battle this past June 21. Let us resist, for August 7 is near. God, the vote, and democracy have spoken; we are going to defend the Constitution and the rule of law as we must. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella has long claimed that he will extradite his predecessor to the United States.

World.title: De la Espriella suspends Colombia’s transfer of power
World.content:
President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella on Tuesday suspended the transfer of power after President Gustavo Petro accused him of fraud.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella said he had “given instructions to the vice president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term.”

I have just given instructions to the president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term, a government that, with its decisions and its conduct, seeks to destroy Colombia. Abelardo de la Espriella

“My duty is to protect the interests of the Nation and guarantee a serious, transparent transition at the service of Colombians, never to legitimize the disaster or the disregard for the constitutional order,” said the president-elect.

In a press conference, Finance Minister German Avila said that he had also suspended cooperation with the transition process in response to comments made by a member of De la Espriella’s team, convicted fraudster Carlos ALonso Lucio, that “undermine the respect, dignity, and decency” of the transition process.

Recent statements by members of the incoming transition committee undermine the respect, dignity, and decency of a process such as the one we are carrying out. These statements were surely made intentionally to hinder the transition process. Accusations and insults have been leveled against the president and his administration, alleging that they are criminals, that they are manipulating the justice system, and that they are seeking to extradite us, among other blunders that have been made. German Avila

“All we have received are insults and disrespect, slander and offenses, and we will not tolerate a single further act of aggression or threat,” said the finance minister.

Avila asked Inspector General Gregorio Eljach to oversee the continuation of the process.

In a post on social media platform X, incoming vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo stressed that his team would continue going through the books to make sure that “those who have betrayed the trust of the Colombian people must answer to the institutions and to history.”

World.content:
Heavy rain, strong winds, and snowfall expected as new frontal system approaches

SANTIAGO â Chile’s central and southern regions are preparing for a powerful frontal system bringing wind, rain, and snow over the coming days, according to updated forecasts from the DirecciÃ³n MeteorolÃ³gica de Chile (DMC). The system is expected to benefit water reserves, with substantial snowfall anticipated across the Andes from the Coquimbo to BiobÃ­o regions.

Gusts may exceed 80 km/h in areas from ValparaÃ­so to Ãuble, driven by a low-level jet stream. Meteorologists are closely monitoring the development of a second system forecast to impact central Chile on Sunday, June 15. Early estimates suggest additional rainfall of up to 40 mm for ValparaÃ­so and the Santiago Metropolitan Region, which may exacerbate soil saturation and pose travel disruptions if storms continue in quick succession.

World.title: Universidad de Chile Eliminated by Curicó Unido in Copa Chile Upset
World.content:
CuricÃ³ Unido advances to quarterfinals after dramatic second-leg draw

SANTIAGO â Defending champions Universidad de Chile have been eliminated from the Copa Chile Coca Cola Sin AzÃºcar 2025 after a 2-2 draw against CuricÃ³ Unido on Wednesday night at Estadio Nacional. The aggregate score favored the visitors, who secured a surprising quarterfinal berth.

Early hopes fade for Universidad de Chile

The home side, managed by Gustavo Ãlvarez, entered the match trailing 2-1 from the first leg. With the return of key players from international duty, including NicolÃ¡s FernÃ¡ndez, MatÃ­as SepÃºlveda, and Maximiliano Guerrero, the team hoped to reverse the deficit.

Universidad de Chile dominated early proceedings, creating multiple chances in the first 15 minutes. However, CuricÃ³ Unido, led by head coach HÃ©ctor Almandoz, resisted pressure and posed threats on the counterattack.

World.title: Chile’s Municipalities, Senapred Meet Ahead of Storm Forecast
World.content:
SANTIAGO, Chile â As Chile prepares for an approaching winter storm system, the Association of Municipalities of Chile (Amuch) held a high-level coordination meeting with the National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (Senapred) to strengthen municipal emergency response measures.

The discussions focused on improving collaboration among municipalities, national agencies, and private service providers to better protect residents during severe weather events.

Power Companies Face Pressure Over Response Times

A central topic in the meeting was the performance of electric utilities during past emergencies. JosÃ© Manuel Palacios, mayor of La Reina, expressed concern over delayed responses from power companies in recent years.

âWe are exploring ways, together with Senapred and other institutions, to develop more efficient actions and hold the companies accountable to meet the response times our residents need,â Palacios said.

Rural Water Supply Risks Tied to Electricity

For rural municipalities, electrical outages pose a dual threat, as potable water systems often rely on electric power. Paula GÃ¡rate, mayor of Melipilla, emphasized the heightened vulnerability of rural areas during storms.

âLosing electricity also means losing access to potable water. Many rural water systems depend on electricity, and that remains our greatest concern,â GÃ¡rate noted.

Coordinated Municipal Efforts to Mitigate Risks

Senapred Director Alicia CebriÃ¡n highlighted the essential role of municipal governments in both preparation and response phases.

âMunicipalities play a crucial role in coordination, information gathering, and implementing mitigation works to reduce the impact of winter threats on residents,â CebriÃ¡n stated.

She underscored that emergency prevention and mitigation is a shared responsibility across public agencies and institutions. âPublic authorities who are directly involved in disaster management bear this responsibility, and we are committed to fulfilling it,â she added.

Winter System Expected to Test Emergency Readiness

The coordination meeting comes as Chileâs central regions brace for a frontal system expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds. Authorities emphasized that ongoing preparation and inter-agency cooperation will be key to minimizing disruption and protecting vulnerable communities.

World.title: Brian Wilson, Legendary Beach Boys Co-Founder, Dies at 82
World.content:
LOS ANGELES â Brian Wilson, the legendary musician, songwriter and co-founder of The Beach Boys, has died at the age of 82, his family announced.

“We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away,” the family said in a statement. “We are at a loss for words right now. Please respect our privacy at this time as our family is grieving. We realize that we are sharing our grief with the world.”

Born in 1942 in Hawthorne, California, Wilson formed The Beach Boys in 1961 with his younger brothers Carl and Dennis, cousin Mike Love, and friend Al Jardine. The band became one of the most influential and commercially successful acts in music history, selling over 100 million records worldwide.

Wilson was the creative force behind the groupâs distinctive harmonies and groundbreaking studio sound. His 1966 album Pet Sounds is regarded as a masterpiece that reshaped the boundaries of pop music production.

Among The Beach Boys’ many hits, Wilson co-wrote and produced I Get Around, Help Me, Rhonda, and Good Vibrations. Rolling Stone ranked The Beach Boys 12th on its list of the “100 Greatest Artists of All Time.”

Tributes poured in following news of his death. Nancy Sinatra shared a photo with Wilson on Instagram, writing, âHis cherished music will live forever as he travels through the Universe and beyond. God bless you, sweet Brian.â

View this post on Instagram A post shared by ð½ðððð¢ ððððððð (@nancysinatra)

Sean Ono Lennon called Wilson the “American Mozart” and a “one of a kind genius from another world,” adding: âAnyone who really knows me knows how heartbroken I am about Brian Wilson passing. Not many people influenced me as much as he did. I feel very lucky that I was able to meet him and spend some time with him. He was always very kind and generous.”

Throughout his life, Wilson faced significant personal struggles. Diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 1984, his condition was linked by doctors to earlier psychedelic drug use. In early 2024, his family revealed he had developed dementia.

Wilson’s wife, Melinda, with whom he shared 24 years of marriage and five adopted children, died earlier in 2024. He also had two daughters, Carnie and Wendy, from his first marriage.

Despite his health battles, Wilsonâs legacy remains unparalleled. His influence on songwriting, vocal harmony, and studio innovation continues to inspire generations of musicians.

World.title: Chile and Norway Deepen Antarctic Cooperation with New Agreement
World.content:
Chile and Norway signed a memorandum of understanding on Antarctic cooperation Monday, reinforcing their shared commitment to peace, science, and environmental protection in the region.

The agreement, signed by Chilean Foreign Minister Alberto van Klaveren and Norwegian Minister of International Development Ã smund GrÃ¸ver, aims to strengthen bilateral coordination under the Antarctic Treaty System. It outlines enhanced collaboration on scientific research, climate monitoring, and the preservation of marine ecosystems through frameworks such as the Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meetings and the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

The accord includes provisions for regular dialogue between scientific and governmental institutions in both countries and seeks to optimize joint efforts in Antarctic and sub-Antarctic research. Both nations also pledged support for the Polar Codeâs implementation, aiming to improve safety and environmental standards for ships operating in polar waters.

Operational and logistical cooperation between Chileâs and Norwayâs national Antarctic programs will also be explored, particularly in alignment with CCAMLRâs conservation objectives.

This renewed alliance builds on the long-standing historical ties between the two nations and reaffirms their role as active stewards of one of the worldâs most fragile and strategically vital environments.

World.title: Full Moon in June 2025: Date, Meaning, and What’s Ahead in the Night Sky
World.content:
The full moon in June 2025 will occur on Wednesday, June 11, and will be visible in most regions depending on local moonrise and moonset times. Known as the Strawberry Moon, this lunar event is tied to Native American traditions marking the ripening of wild strawberries and the approach of summer in the Northern Hemisphere.

In Argentina, for example, the moon will rise around 5:52 p.m. and set at 9:19 a.m. on June 12. This full moon, like others throughout the year, has long held cultural, astrological, and even emotional significance. While there is no scientific consensus on its effects, itâs commonly associated with heightened emotions, sleep disturbances, and symbolic transitions.
