World.title: Croatia Airlines to Serve Authentic Dalmatian Flavours from August
World.content:
July the 24th, 2026 – Croatia Airlines is set to serve its passengers authentic Dalmatian flavours as of August the 1st this year.

Passengers flying on Croatia Airlines planes will be treated to a genuine taste of Dalmatia before they even land as the national carrier launches a new onboard gastronomic offer. Poslovni reports that as of August the 1st, Dalmatian flavours will be able to be enjoyed before the aircraft’s wheels even touch Croatian soil. The move is primarily designed to showcase this special region of Croatia’s local food producers and rich culinary traditions.

The new initiative is part of a collaboration between Croatia Airlines, the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board and the county itself. The aim is to introduce travellers to authentic Dalmatian products during their flight, creating a unique welcome experience while promoting this coastal region’s food, culture and local businesses.

Passengers will receive specially curated snack packages featuring a selection of products made by producers from the Split-Dalmatia region. The project is intended not only to enhance the in-flight experience but also to encourage visitors to explore local gastronomy once they arrive at their destination.

Those within tourism have claimed that food and drink have become an increasingly important part of the travel experience, with many visitors choosing destinations based on their culinary heritage. By bringing regional flavours on board, Croatia Airlines hopes to strengthen the connection between air travel and Croatia’s tourism offer while supporting local producers.

The programme follows similar regional collaborations introduced by the airline, which has already featured products from other Croatian destinations as part of its efforts to highlight the country’s diverse gastronomic heritage.

The new Dalmatian snack selection will be available on Croatia Airlines flights as of the first day of August, giving passengers an opportunity to sample a taste of one of Croatia’s most popular tourist regions before their holiday even begins.

World.title: Working From Home in Croatia Remains Rare Compared to Europe
World.content:
July the 24th, 2026 – Working from home boomed during the coronavirus pandemic, with the world altering tremendously in that regard, but it still remains rare in Croatia.

Working from home remains the exception rather than the rule across Croatia, with the country ranking near the bottom of the entire European Union for remote work despite the widespread adoption of flexible working models elsewhere across the continent.

According to the latest Eurostat data, only a small share of employed people in Croatia usually work from home, placing the country among the EU’s lowest-ranked nations. By comparison, countries such as Finland and Ireland have embraced remote work on a much larger scale, with around one in five employees regularly working from home. The EU average is close to 9 percent.

The figures highlight a growing divide between northern and southern Europe. While remote and hybrid work have become firmly established in many countries since the COVID-19 pandemic, Croatia has largely returned to traditional office-based working patterns. Analysts point out that the country’s economic structure plays a significant role, as many of Croatia’s largest industries—including tourism, hospitality, retail, construction and manufacturing—require employees to be physically present at work.

Another factor is company culture. Many Croatian employers continue to favour in-person work, particularly in small and medium-sized businesses where remote work policies have been slower to develop. Even in sectors where working from home is technically possible, employers often prefer office attendance over flexible arrangements.

The data also reflects how unevenly remote work has developed across Europe. Finland leads the bloc, followed by Ireland, while countries such as Romania, Bulgaria and Greece record the lowest shares. Croatia sits much closer to that group than to the EU average, underlining how limited remote work remains in the country.

Experts note that hybrid working is more common than the statistics suggest, as Eurostat’s methodology counts only people who usually work from home for at least half of their working time. Employees who occasionally work remotely but spend most of the week in the office are not included in the headline figures.

Although flexible working arrangements continue to expand across many parts of Europe, Croatia’s labour market remains heavily office- and workplace-based. Whether that changes in the coming years is likely to depend on employer attitudes, investment in digital jobs, and the continued growth of sectors where remote work is a practical option.

World.title: Europa League Qualifiers: Hajduk Beats Pafos 2-0 in First Leg
World.content:
Hajduk hosted Cyprus’s Pafos at Poljud tonight in the first leg of the Europa League second qualifying round. Having knocked out Slovakia’s Žilina in the first round, the Split side faced a tough task against a team that competed in the Champions League last season.

Should Gonzalo Garcia’s side get past Pafos, they’ll face Austria’s Salzburg in the third qualifying round, while the losing side drops into the Conference League third qualifying round, taking on the winner of the tie between Georgia’s Dinamo Tbilisi and Lithuania’s Žalgiris.

Lineups

Hajduk: Silić; Acapandie, Marešić, Van Hoorenbeeck, Hrgović — Pajaziti, Pukštas — Brajković, Dalisson, Melnjak — Šego

Pafos: Majecki; Mmaee, Luiz, Goldar — Ioannou, Šunjić, Pepe, Jaja — Gabriel Teixeira, Dragomir, Lele

Match report

Pafos threatened early on when Pajaziti lost the ball in midfield in the 4th minute and pulled back Teixeira to stop the counter, picking up the game’s first yellow card in the process.

Hajduk responded with a promising move in the 5th minute, as Šego laid the ball back to Melnjak, who left it for Hrgović, though Pafos managed to cut the move short before it could develop.

Hajduk had their first real sight of goal in the 8th minute, when a dangerous free-kick from Šego cannoned off the defensive wall and out for a corner.

Pafos threatened in the 15th minute, when a long-range free-kick was met by Goldar’s header, but Silić dealt with it comfortably. Hajduk’s early total dominance eased slightly by the 18th minute, when Pepe’s long-range effort drifted harmlessly over the bar.

Hrgović and Melnjak combined well down the left in the 21st minute to get in behind the Pafos defense, but Hrgović’s low ball into the middle failed to find a teammate.

The game grew more even by the 29th minute, though Pafos still hadn’t created a genuine chance of their own. Hajduk came desperately close in the 25th minute, when Melnjak whipped in a superb ball to the box for Šego, who was a fraction late arriving and couldn’t quite get enough on it to test the keeper.

Dalisson showed good feet between two defenders in the 31st minute, feeding the ball left to Hrgović, who curled an effort towards the far post from an angle — somewhere between a shot and a cross.

Poljud rang with whistles in the 35th minute after Dalisson went down under a challenge, followed by a foul awarded against Pajaziti in a similar situation moments later, with the Albanian, already on a yellow card, now needing to be careful.

Hajduk almost broke through again in the 41st minute, when Hrgović whipped in another sharp delivery from the left towards the far post, but Šego couldn’t quite connect with a sliding effort.

Pafos had a sight of goal in the 43rd minute, when Dragomir’s corner found David Luiz, but his header lacked any real danger.

Only one minute of stoppage time was played before the referee brought the first half to a close.

The second half got underway with no changes to either side.

Hajduk won a dangerous free-kick in the 55th minute when Ioannou fouled Brajković and was booked for his troubles, handing Hajduk a chance from a threatening position.

They made it count immediately. In the 56th minute, Šego stepped up to the resulting free-kick from around 20 meters and beat the Pafos goalkeeper with the aid of the crossbar — Hajduk led 1-0!

Pafos made a double change in the 62nd minute, with Pepe and Goldar making way for Brito and Bruno.

Hajduk doubled their lead just three minutes later. In the 65th minute, Acapandie and Dalisson combined with a slick one-two down the right, and Acapandie’s ball into the middle was turned home with a brilliant reaction finish from Melnjak’s left foot — 2-0 to Hajduk!

Pafos took the initiative in the 70th minute and pushed forward with everything they had, but Hajduk’s defense held firm.

Pafos made another double change in the 74th minute, with Šunjić and Dragomir replaced by Quina and Rodrigues.

Garcia responded with a triple substitution of his own in the 77th minute, bringing on Livaja, Skelin and Del Moral for Šego, Marešić and Dalisson — with Livaja’s introduction greeted by a thunderous ovation from the stands.

Huram replaced Melnjak in the 82nd minute. Hajduk’s defense continued to hold firm. Pafos pressed but had yet to fashion a genuine chance.

In the 87th minute, Huram received a yellow card.

Three minutes of stoppage time were added, and Pafos had one last chance with a free kick just outside the box, but it was an easy clear for Hajduk.



The game finished 2-0. The second leg is next Thursday, July 30th, in Paphos.

World.title: Iraq accelerates journey towards WTO membership
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has increased its attempts to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), with the new administration advancing a process that officials regard as part of a larger agenda of economic reform and diversification.

Iraq’s accession to the WTO would bring it into the rules-based global trading system, compelling the country to match its trade policies with international norms for market access, transparency, and regulation.

While membership does not ensure economic development, many observers regard it as a significant step toward building a more predictable climate for trade and investment.

Iraq’s WTO entrance is part of broader attempts to promote private sector growth, attract international investment, and boost non-oil economic activity. The process also requires considerable legal and institutional changes, such as modernizing trade laws and improving regulatory frameworks.

Last week, a team from Iraq’s Ministry of Trade traveled to Geneva to finalize technical documents with the WTO Accession Division and the International Trade Centre (ITC), marking another step forward in the country’s accession discussions.

Since 2020, the ITC has been supporting Iraq’s WTO accession process through a European Union-funded program.

Its work has focused on providing technical assistance to Iraqi institutions as they prepare for negotiations and implement the reforms required by the accession process.

Beyond the discussions, WTO admission is usually seen as a long-term reform goal.

The process promotes greater transparency, more predictable trade policies, and stronger institutions, while assisting countries in aligning domestic regulations with internationally recognized trade rules.

These measures might help Iraq diversify its economy, enhance its business environment, and integrate more effectively into regional and global value networks.

Their success, however, will be dependent on ongoing political commitment and execution after admission.

As negotiations continue, Iraq’s accession process remains both a trade negotiation and a larger exercise in economic modernization, with assistance from the WTO Secretariat, the ITC, the Ministry of Trade, and the European Union.

World.title: Ukraine hits ‘Russia’s Amazon’ warehouses outside St Petersburg
World.content:
Saint Petersburg – Ukrainian drones Friday hit warehouses for Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries for a third time in six days, this time near Saint Petersburg, triggering a fire that sent smoke pouring over the historic city.

Kyiv has accused Wildberries — Russia’s largest online retailer often known as the Russian equivalent of Amazon — of storing drone parts and helping the Russian army.

Ukraine has targeted Saint Petersburg as it steps up long-range drone strikes on Russian energy, military and logistics sites in recent weeks, calling the attacks justified retribution for Moscow’s nightly drone and missile barrage of its cities.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down some 571 drones overnight over more than a dozen regions and Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014 — one of the largest one-night barrages of the war.

In Saint Petersburg, an AFP reporter saw grey smoke rising into the morning sky over high-rise residential buildings in the city, President Vladimir Putin’s hometown that is more than 800 kilometres (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Wildberries said two of its logistics facilities in Saint Petersburg and one in Simferopol, in Moscow-annexed Crimea, were hit.

“Rapid evacuation was carried out at all the warehouses … according to preliminary data, there are no casualties,” Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim said on social media.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region said three people were wounded in the attack, which saw at least 59 drones fired towards Saint Petersburg.

It was the third overnight attack by Ukraine on Wildberries’ sites in the past week.

Last weekend, eight night-shift workers were killed in attacks on Wildberries sites that saw one of the company’s main warehouses outside Moscow burn to the ground.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged after the first attack that the facilities were used to “supply sanctioned components for drone production and navigation equipment.”

Hundreds of small businesses saw their inventories wiped out in the strike, triggering angry comments on social media.

Kyiv calls its strikes “long-range sanctions”, saying the attacks are justified retribution for Russia’s more than four-year offensive and nightly attacks on its cities.

The campaign has triggered nationwide fuel shortages and, Kyiv says, dented Russia’s financial war chest.

– ‘Escalation’ –

Columns of thick black smoke were still billowing into the sky from one of the factories hours after the hit, an AFP reporter saw.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spent the first years of the war trying to shield the population from the fall-out of his decision to launch the offensive on Ukraine.

But the strikes on oil refineries have triggered fuel shortages and big attacks near major cities have brought the dramatic visible consequences of the war into the homes of many Russians.

Firefighters and investigators had been deployed to the sites in Saint Petersburg as the blaze raged through the morning, Russian officials said.

Saint Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport suspended flights during the attack, resuming operations around 06:00 (0300 GMT), with around 50 departures disrupted.

Both Russia and Ukraine have escalated their long-range strikes in recent months.

Moscow’s forces have fired increasing numbers of ballistic missiles at Kyiv — killing dozens and ripping open apartment blocks.

US President Donald Trump has appeared to give his backing to Ukraine’s counter-attacks on Russia — calling the strikes “an escalation that can lead to an end”.

Washington’s attempts to mediate a peace deal between the warring sides have largely stalled with its own war on Iran raging.

The United Nations has reported a surge in civilian deaths in 2026, saying June was the deadliest month since mid-2022.

Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and tens of thousands of civilians have been killed since Russia launched its full-scale offensive in February 2022 — though there is no precise toll with neither side routinely revealing the number of their losses.

World.title: South Korean tycoon ordered to pay $644m in divorce
World.content:
Seoul – A South Korean court ordered an AI chip-manufacturing tycoon on Friday to make a trimmed-down $644 million divorce payment to his former wife.

Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix — a pillar of South Korea’s tech-led economy.

Seoul High Court in 2024 had told him to pay 1.38 trillion won ($940 million) to his ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong, daughter of a former South Korea president.

The sum — equal to more than $1 billion at the exchange rate at the time of the ruling — led local media to dub it the “divorce of the century”.

Chey appealed to the Supreme Court, which told the high court to reconsider its 2024 decision and led to the tycoon’s reduced divorce bill of 944 billion won ($644 million).

The settlement is not yet final, however, as either side may refer it back to the Supreme Court.

The acrimonious case centres on the definition and valuation of the couple’s shared assets, including Chey’s lucrative stake in the SK Group.

Seoul High Court ruled Friday that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple’s marital assets.

“The defendant’s shareholdings increased substantially during the marriage through his management activities,” the court said.

“The plaintiff contributed to that increase through homemaking, childcare and public-facing activities related to SK Group.”

Chey and Roh married in 1988, but the couple are believed to have lived apart for more than 15 years. In 2015 he admitted to fathering a child with his lover.

With SK hynix selling vital memory chips to AI computing company Nvidia, Chey’s stake is now worth roughly $5.5 billion, according to regulatory filings and public data.

Roh, 65, has three children with Chey and has built a career in the cultural space, running a digital art museum.

– Bribes –

The pair were wed in Seoul’s presidential Blue House when her father Roh Tae-woo led the country from 1988 to 1993.

They have battled over the split in the courts since 2022, after Chey filed for divorce in 2017 and mediation broke down.

The court’s original 2024 ruling ordering the payout to Roh cited a 30 billion won slush fund her ex-president father used to propel SK Group’s growth.

The court said at the time that could be counted as her contribution towards the couple’s shared assets.

But in October last year the Supreme Court quashed that argument, saying that any such cash likely stemmed from illegal bribes and therefore should not be counted.

Another question was whether the dramatic increase in SK Group’s value since the couple’s separation, on the cusp of the AI boom, should be reflected in the asset division.

“The court took into account the sharp rise in the value of the defendant’s shareholdings when determining the property division ratio,” Friday’s court statement said.

SK Group shares have more than tripled in value since December 2015, when Chey publicly disclosed his extramarital affair.

The Supreme Court had already separately ordered Chey to make an alimony payment to Roh of 2 billion won.

World.title: PepsiCo deepens Iraq partnership with manufacturing, agriculture deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PepsiCo has inked agreements with two Iraqi partners to increase food and beverage production, boost agricultural supply chains, and create employment, adding to a string of US investments announced during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington.

The agreements, inked during the U.S.-Iraq High-Level Business Summit organized by the US Chamber of Commerce, strengthen PepsiCo’s collaborations with Baghdad Soft Drinks Company (BSDC), its long-standing bottling partner in Iraq, and Green Iraq Company (GICO).

According to the deal with BSDC, PepsiCo will aim to increase yearly production capacity to more than 250 million beverage cases, maintaining Iraq’s position as one of the company’s major manufacturing and bottling centers in the Middle East.

The expansion is planned to create new employment in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, and distribution, as well as teach and provide technical skills to Iraqi engineers and technicians.

A separate deal with GICO seeks to increase food production capacity and agricultural productivity by bringing advanced irrigation methods and farming practices to local farmers, therefore boosting Iraq’s goal to become a regional food and beverage export center.

According to PepsiCo, the program aims to boost domestic supply chains by encouraging more local procurement and assisting Iraqi farmers in improving yields and sustainability.

The deals were part of a series of commercial understandings struck at the summit, in which US and Iraqi firms announced commitments in energy, banking, aviation, infrastructure, and manufacturing as Baghdad strives to diversify its economy away from oil and attract foreign investment.

Baghdad Soft Drinks Company has been working with PepsiCo for over four decades, and both agreements were signed on behalf of BSDC and GICO by majority stakeholder Tarek Al Hassan.

The investment demonstrates global firms’ rising interest in Iraq’s consumer products industry, as improved economic circumstances and government reforms stimulate more private sector investment and industrial growth.

World.title: Socceroos star Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine
World.content:
Sydney – Australian World Cup star Cristian Volpato allegedly tested positive for cocaine after he was pulled over for speeding in Sydney on Friday, police and reports said.

A New South Wales police statement said a 22-year-old man — widely identified as Italy-based Volpato by local media — was allegedly caught speeding twice overnight.

He passed a roadside breath test on the first occasion and was issued an infringement notice before being pulled over again two hours later.

This time he was drug tested and returned a positive result for cocaine, police claimed, with a second sample sent for further analysis.

“His international driver’s licence was suspended for a period of six months, withdrawing his driving privileges in NSW,” police said.

Volpato, who plays for Serie A side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup after switching his international allegiance from Italy to Australia shortly before the tournament.

He was born and raised in Sydney before moving overseas and represented Italy at various youth levels.

Tony Basha, a Sydney-based coach who trained Volpato before he moved to Italy and remains a mentor, told the Sydney Morning Herald the attacking midfielder denied taking cocaine or any other illicit substance.

“He was adamant he didn’t touch it,” Basha said. “He was shocked. I’m shocked because it’s a big allegation.”

World.title: Volkswagen profit plunges as carmaker weighs mass job cuts
World.content:
Frankfurt – Volkswagen said Friday that its net profit plunged in the second quarter as the crisis-hit carmaker, weighing up to 100,000 job cuts worldwide, grapples with increasing competition in and from China.

Net profit for the three months to the end of June came in at 1.54 billion euros ($1.75 billion), the 10-brand group said, a fall of 32.9 percent on the same period last year. Last year’s figure was itself a decline of almost 37 percent on 2024.

The result was hit by a 500-million-euro charge the carmaker booked for stopping US production of its electric ID.4, Volkswagen said, as well as “negative mix effects”, meaning the automotive giant sold more lower-margin products.

The firm, which in addition to its own brand also includes the likes of Lamborghini, Audi, Skoda and Porsche, also cut its guidance for the year and said it now saw sales flat or falling up to three percent. It previously expected growth of up to three percent.

The results pile pressure on the beleaguered group, which has been suffering from slimmer margins from the sales of electric cars, US tariffs and above all intense Chinese competition.

“We must accelerate efforts to structurally lower our cost base and sustainably improve our earnings quality,” Volkswagen finance chief Arno Antlitz said. “What matters now is swift and consistent implementation.”

World.title: Iraq border in focus as Kuwait reports drone attack
World.content:
Dubai – Here are the main events related to the war in the Middle East:

– Iran blasts Trump assets threat –

Tehran said Friday that US President Donald Trump’s threat to pay for shipping damage with Iranian assets was an “incendiary precedent”.

Trump had said that Washington would start using frozen Iranian assets “that the United States has in its possession, and controls” to pay for “any and all damages done to Ships, Cargo or anything related” in the region.

– New US strikes –

The United States military said Thursday it was attacking Iran for the 13th night in a row, adding that strikes were aimed at military targets with the goal of diminishing Iranian ability to attack shipping.

Iranian state media reported that US missiles had hit the city of Ahvaz, near the border with Iraq, and explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas on the Strait of Hormuz and in Omidiyeh.

– Kuwait under attack –

Kuwaiti air defences have opened fire on incoming Iranian missiles and drones, hours after reporting a new drone attack at the border crossing with Iraq.

“Kuwaiti air defences are currently intercepting hostile missile and drone attacks following the wrongful Iranian aggression,” the general staff said in a message posted on social media.

– Trump rebuked –

The US House of Representatives passed a largely symbolic resolution calling for President Donald Trump to halt military action against Iran, delivering another congressional rebuke as the Middle East war escalates.

The measure directs Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorises the war.

– Houthi attacks ‘illegal’ –

Attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea by Yemen’s Houthi militants have drawn condemnation from around Europe.

Germany said the attacks risked escalating conflicts, Britain condemned the group’s “reckless actions” and EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas said the attacks were “unacceptable” and “illegal”.

– UN chief warning –

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said the Middle East conflict was “getting out of control”.

“It is teetering on the edge of the unimaginable,” he said.

– Oil passes $100 –

The price of the benchmark international oil contract, Brent North Sea soared more than eight percent to reach $101.93 a barrel after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The main US oil contract, West Texas Intermediate, rose 7.6 percent to $93.44 a barrel.

– Island strike –

Iranian news outlet Tasnim reported that a US missile had hit a site near the town of Suza on Qeshm Island, in the disputed Strait of Hormuz.

– Trump threatens Houthis –

Trump threatened Yemen’s Houthi rebels with “major military punishment” after they launched missile and drone strikes at oil tankers in the Red Sea.

“The US will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis themselves” should the rebels launch further attacks, Trump said on his Truth Social network.

– Britain withdraws Iran staff –

Britain said it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran.

“Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely,” the foreign ministry said on its website.

World.title: Kuwait blames Iran afters drones hit border with Iraq
World.content:
Kuwait City — Kuwait on Thursday said drones hit its side of the border with Iraq, with one Kuwaiti official telling AFP Iran was to blame.

“The Al-Abdali border crossing was attacked this afternoon by hostile drones, resulting in material damage, but thankfully no casualties,” defense ministry spokesman Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan said in a statement.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed the incident prior to the ministry’s statement.

World.title: Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3
World.content:
JAMMU: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic on the third consecutive day.

The suspension of all major pilgrimages in the Union Territory â Amarnath, Vaishno Devi, Machhail Mata, Shiv Khori and Sarthal Mata Yatras â in place since July 19, continued for the sixth day.

Officials said the NH was blocked at Deohal bridge, Samroli and Jakhani in Udhampur district, and Banihal in Ramban district. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure.

Amid concerns of fresh landslides and shooting stones along the stretch, officials urged commuters not to travel on the road until it was declared safe for movement.

Kishtwar district magistrate, in an order issued Friday, barred all movement along the Kishtwar-Paddar-Gulabgarh axis from July 25-27 â in view of rain-triggered safety hazards along the stretch, such as slippery road conditions, landslips and persistent shooting stones â until further notice.





All ceremonial and customary religious rituals associated with the Machhail Mata Yatra shall be performed symbolically, the order stated, advising pilgrims and the public against venturing towards Gulabgarh or Machhail between July 25-27.

Rain-triggered flash floods struck Barkuanda area in Bupp, Udhampur, early Friday, affecting several households. There were no casualties. Damage assessment was underway, officials said.

World.title: Haryana’s air pollution action plan: Centre suggests strict enforcement and accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
World.content:
Centre reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR, and emphasised the need for âaccelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcementâ to ensure substantial reduction in pollution before the onset of the winter season when stubble burning and meteorological conditions raise the levels of pollutants.The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on Haryanaâs air pollution action plan and multiple steps, which are being taken, with particular focus on legacy waste, road dust, industrial pollution and strengthening the infrastructure to enable accelerated EV adoption.Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and senior officials of the state govt attended the meeting."The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality,â said Yadav while emphasising the urgency of timely action.On critical issue of stubble burning that increases level of air pollutants in Delhi-NCR during every winter, Yadav urged the state govt to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres.He also emphasised the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. He suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats, and asked District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management.âThe state authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers,â said a statement from the environment ministry on the review meeting.It said, âThe minister also reviewed progress on construction and demolition waste management and requested that the establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of legacy waste should be undertaken on a war footing.âReferring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and biomass burning, Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100% collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning.On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the âParivartanâ scheme.âThe minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the âNo PUCC, No Fuelâ initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Yadav asked the authorities to identify traffic congestion hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest,â said the official statement.Reviewing industrial pollution control measures, Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units.

World.title: Police identify 2,500 people with criminal records at Jantar Mantar protest through facial recognition cameras
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around the protest site at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

"The technology has so far helped identify over 2,500 persons with criminal antecedents. It acts as a strong deterrent and allows us to keep a close watch on those who may attempt to misuse the protest to create law and order problems," sources told PTI.

According to the sources, the FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database.

"The objective is to ensure that people with criminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources told PTI.

"The system is connected with the Delhi Police database and can identify wanted criminals, absconders, history-sheeters, and Bad Characters (BCs) whose details already exist in police records," they added.

According to an officer, the FRS does not target ordinary protesters but is meant to identify those with criminal antecedents who may attempt to take advantage of large gatherings."

These are high-resolution cameras capable of capturing facial images even from a distance.





Once a face is captured, it is quickly matched with the police database. If a wanted or absconding accused is detected, the concerned police unit is immediately alerted, and legal action can be initiated without delay," he said.

Police said the technology will also help identify habitual offenders who have repeatedly figured in criminal cases and are listed as "Bad Characters" in Delhi Police records."

The deployment acts as both a preventive and investigative tool. It helps us remain alert against anti-social elements who may try to infiltrate the protest, create a nuisance, or disturb law and order," another officer said.

The installation of the FRS forms part of enhanced security arrangements around Jantar Mantar.

World.title: 'Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday thanked young people for watching his video on examination reforms and sharing their suggestions.

In a video message shared on Instagram, PM Modi expressed appreciation for the response to his address and the feedback received from students and young people.

"Thank you friends. I had the opportunity to meet you late last night. I appreciate the way you responded to my video and your positive suggestions. Thanks to everyone..." PM Modi said.

"Last night, I got the opportunity to interact with you. The way you responded to the video I posted and shared your positive suggestionsâthanks to everybody. Your love and support continue, and that our connection grows even stronger and more active," he further said.

The caption of the video read: "Thanks to the youngsters who watched my video yesterday and sent insightful suggestions."

PM Modi's message comes a day after he announced that the government would introduce stricter measures to tackle examination paper leaks amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.

In a video message on Thursday, PM Modi said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill providing for fast-track courts and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases, with efforts to pass the legislation in Parliament during the coming week.





"I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakhs of students and their guardians," the Prime Minister had said, adding that the government had already arrested those responsible and ensured that nearly 22 lakh students were able to retake the examination without losing an academic year.

He had also said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher penalties to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.

The announcement came amid widespread protests over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. Earlier this week, PM Modi also told the NDA Parliamentary Party that the government was working to make the country's examination system "foolproof".

World.title: Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the merchant vessel MV Golden Leo, which was struck in a Russian attack off Ukraine's Odesa port earlier this week, was carrying grain and not military cargo, effectively rejecting Moscow's assertion that the ship was transporting weapons for Ukraine.

Responding to questions on the Russian claim, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the information available with the Indian government showed the Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel had loaded grain before leaving Odesa.

"As per information made available to us from the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, India, MV Golden Leo, the Guinea-Bissau-flagged commercial vessel involved in the tragic incident in the Odesa port, had loaded grain as cargo prior to its departure on July 19," Jaiswal said at the ministry's weekly media briefing.

"We once again reiterate that commercial shipping and seafarers must not be targeted under any circumstances," he added.

The clarification came days after a Russian strike on the merchant vessel killed 10 people, including four Indian seafarers, marking the first deaths of Indian sailors since the Russia-Ukraine war began.

India reiterates concerns to Russia

Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated India's position during his meeting with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila on Wednesday.





India had also summoned Russian Charge d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov on Tuesday to convey its "grave concerns" and "unequivocal condemnation" of the attack on the commercial vessel.

The move followed remarks by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who defended Russia's actions, saying Moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for Ukraine.

Peskov said Russian forces would continue striking ships involved in transporting "ammunition, weapons, and so on" for the Kyiv government.

India's latest statement, citing cargo details provided by the directorate general of maritime administration, contradicts that assertion.

Shipping attacks under scrutiny

MV Golden Leo, carrying 17 crew members including five Indians, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

The attack has intensified India's concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the conflict zone.

Separately, the MEA also condemned another attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping "unacceptable" and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and the uninterrupted flow of global trade.

With two fatal incidents involving Indian seafarers in less than a week, India has repeatedly stressed that civilian merchant vessels and their crews must not be targeted during the ongoing conflict.

World.title: Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending
World.content:
Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending

BENGALURU: At a time when Centre has announced setting up of Fast-Track Courts (FTC) to ensure expeditious trials in paper leak cases in the wake of the 2026 NEET fiasco, the countryâs Fast-Track Special Courts (FTSCs) â operating under the most recent scheme introduced in Oct 2019 â are buckling under mounting backlogs.Govt data analysed by TOI shows that annual disposals by FTSCs, created to deliver swift justice in some of the most sensitive criminal cases (rape and Pocso), dropped to 66,500 cases in 2025, down from a record 85,595 in 2024, a decline of more than 22%. At the same time, pending cases rose from a little more than 2 lakh at the end of 2024 to nearly 2.5 lakh by the close of 2025.The trend suggests that despite expanding judicial capacity, fresh cases continue to outnumber disposals. Since 2021, pendency has increased by nearly one-third, from around 1.8 lakh to nearly 2.5 lakh , even as annual disposals almost doubled between 2021 and 2024 before falling last year.The figures point to a structural challenge rather than a temporary slowdown. Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice, but rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards.The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.As per the latest information from the govt, the FTSC scheme currently operates 775 courts, including 398 exclusive POCSO courts, across the country. This is against a target of at least 790 courts that should have been functional. The courts have disposed of nearly 3.9 lakh cases since inception. Yet with nearly 2.5 lakh cases still pending, the gains have not translated into a sustained reduction in backlog.The experience varies widely across States. While some States have managed comparatively low pendency per court, others continue to operate under far heavier workloads, indicating that the effectiveness of the scheme depends not only on the number of courts but also on staffing, infrastructure and the volume of new cases entering the system.The latest figures relate specifically to Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), which are a separate scheme launched by the Centre in Oct 2019 to hear rape and Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases, which has since been extended up to Sept 30, 2026. These should not be confused with the original Fast Track Courts (FTCs), which were introduced nearly two decades earlier â 880 of which are functional currently.These courts had disposed of more than 13 lakh cases in 2025, up from 11.7 lakh in 2024, but lower than 15.2 lakh in 2023. However, year-wise pendency data on FTCs wasnât immediately available. The department of justiceâs dashboard, which was accessible as of July 23 night, was offline on Friday.History Of Fast-Track CourtsIndiaâs first FTCs were established in 2000 following the recommendations of the 11th Finance Commission. The idea was to create additional courts on a temporary basis to clear long-pending sessions cases and reduce the number of undertrial prisoners.The Centre funded the scheme until March 31, 2011, after which States were expected to use their own resources. While several States retained or expanded FTCs, others allowed them to lapse, leading to wide variations across the country.The policy then evolved after the 2012 Nirbhaya case, as public pressure mounted for quicker trials in sexual offence cases. The 14th Finance Commission later supported the creation of 1,800 Fast Track Courts using the increased fiscal space available to States, though without dedicated central funding.And, in Oct 2019 the FTSCs scheme under the Nirbhaya Fund was launched. Since then, the ordinary FTCs remain the responsibility of state govts and high courts, while the Centre funds only the FTSC scheme.

World.title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
World.content:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.

World.title: Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA-Rasayan) scheme for establishing three dedicated chemical parks in the country.

The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, of which Rs 3,000 crore will be used for establishing common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities inside the parks, while the remaining Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for administrative expenditure.

Announced in the Union Budget, the scheme will run for five years. While the Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park, the state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.

Govt said the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme is expected to promote the development of the chemical industry and its value chain, including upstream, downstream and ancillary industries, while ensuring efficient utilisation of resources.

By providing shared common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities tailored to the needs of the chemical industry, the scheme is expected to enhance cost competitiveness and make the Indian chemical industry globally competitive. It will also help the sector integrate better with global value chains, boosting exports and import substitution.

The scheme will create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralised facilities such as a common effluent treatment plant, treatment, storage and disposal facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. Govt said the development of the chemical sector will generate employment and contribute to economic growth.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: PM Modi thanks people for 'insightful' suggestions on video in another Instagram reel
World.content:
The government and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held talks on Friday (July 24, 2026) at the Constitution Club of India after the Centre “agreed” to the CJP’s demand that the meeting be held at a neutral venue.

The CJP has said the “strictest action” the government could take against examination irregularities was to remove Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement that a Bill providing for stringent action against paper leaks would be introduced in Parliament.

Also Read: PM reaches out to students; Sonam Wangchuk ends fast

The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is “verifying media reports” on the use of pellet guns by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) against unarmed protesters during July 20 march to Parliament in New Delhi, an official said on Friday (July 24, 2026). This comes three days after The Hindu reported the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in the national capital.

Also Read: Student protests are the consequence of Modi government’s policies, writes Sonia Gandhi

Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his indefinite hunger strike after the government assured him that his demands would be met. He announced the end of his fast after Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at the Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around Thursday (July 23, 2026) midnight and conveyed the government’s assurances.

World.title: ‘How dare you threaten students?’: Jamia, JNU face backlash over protest advisories
World.content:
NEW DELHI

A day after Delhi University (DU) issued a similar advisory, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) and Jamia Millia Islamia issued advisories asking students to “refrain from participating” in gatherings in and around Jantar Mantar, adding that violations may invite legal consequences as well as disciplinary action.

The advisories drew sharp criticism from Opposition leaders, who said they would have a “chilling effect on democratic speech and expression”.

‘Legal consequences’

In its advisory, JNU stated: “Please exercise responsibility on social media. Violations may invite legal consequences under applicable laws as well as disciplinary action under the University’s code of conduct.”

By evening, Jamia also issued an advisory on social media, stating that students worked hard and travelled from across the country to study at the university. It added: “Nothing is worth placing at risk a future nurtured through such hard work, dedication and sacrifice.”

“In keeping with the assurances of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India himself that the interests of the students shall be safeguarded and stern action will be taken against those who have played with the future of the students, JMI appeals to all its students and stakeholders to refrain from any activity that is not in keeping with the law,” it added. The advisory asked students to focus on their studies.

‘Exercising their rights’

Responding to the JNU advisory, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said, “How dare you threaten students for exercising their democratic rights? Please note, you are the ones who will be held accountable when the time comes.”

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said that instead of making Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign and then start a meaningful discussion on the education system, “Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have resorted to denigrating the centres of learning”.

Party MP Shashi Tharoor reacted to DU’s advisory, saying that even during the days of the JP Movement leading up to the Emergency in 1975, there was no bar on DU students protesting. He said, “A university is meant to teach critical thinking and independent assessment of issues, not to stifle these very qualities.”

He argued that most DU students were not privileged enough to ignore such a sternly worded warning without fearing consequences to their academic or professional prospects if they attended the protests.

Congress MP and general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal called the advisories a “travesty”, saying that DU and JNU had a long history of fostering healthy debate and shaping India’s political discourse. “These universities should withdraw these circulars at the earliest. They are blatantly unconstitutional,” he said.

The advisories also drew criticism from students, who pointed out that their universities had a history of student movements and said the latest advisories showed that the institutions were now “compromised”.

‘Act of intimidation’

The JNU Students’ Union (JNUSU) condemned the “anti-democratic and anti-constitutional” advisory, calling it a “blatant act of intimidation designed to silence dissent”. It added that the ongoing youth movement was a culmination of a decade of suppression and crackdown on dissent.

“Rising unemployment, shrinking expenditure on education, and a relentless spate of paper leaks have left students with no option but to take to the streets. JNUSU stands firmly with this movement and with the youth of this nation, who continue to march despite lathi charges, tear gas, water cannons, firing and pellet guns,” it said in a statement.

World.title: Delhi Police set up STF to probe exam-related offences, paper leaks
World.content:
The Delhi police have constituted a special task force (STF) within the Crime Branch to investigate paper leaks and other examination-related offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, a senior officer said on Friday. According to the officer, the STF will be headed by an officer of the rank of Deputy Commissioner of Police in the Crime Branch.

It will investigate offences related to public examinations conducted by various bodies, including the Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission and the National Testing Agency.

The STF will also investigate offences related to recruitment examinations conducted by ministries and departments of the Central government, as well as their attached and subordinate offices, the officer said.

“The task force will investigate offences involving any other authority notified by the Central government from time to time. Besides investigating cases, the STF will coordinate with prosecuting agencies to ensure expeditious prosecution and facilitate the day-to-day conduct of trials in such cases,” the officer added.

World.title: Did not cut any deal with government: Sonam Wangchuk
World.content:
After being criticised by several social media users for ending his hunger strike in the presence of Union Ministers, activist Sonam Wangchuk released a long video message on Friday (July 24, 2026) where he asserted that he “did not cut any deal” with the government and ended the fast as he feared a crackdown against students and protestors at Jantar Mantar.

He said he did not press for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan as it is inevitable due to the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar and movement by the youth across the country. He ended the fast around 12:30 a.m. Friday (July 24), in the presence of Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh, his wife and civil society leaders from Ladakh. Mr. Nadda served him soup to end the strike.

“Instead, I focused on getting justice for the students and young people against whom FIRs have been registered. We saw what happened after the Ladakh incident on September 24, 2025: around 80 people were arrested and thrown in jails. For me, the future of these young people is more important. Government wasn’t ready to give a written assurance, but I refused to end my hunger strike without this key point being included in the agreement,”

Releasing a 24:22-minute video from Medanta Hospital, where he is still under observation, Mr. Wangchuk said he wanted the members of Opposition as well as the CJP to be present, but the “agencies” did not agree.

AFTER 26 DAYS OF HUNGER DO I NEED TO PROVE MY SINCERITY !!!

Do please watch and help spread the word. Find the full 22 minutes video on my YouTube Channel: Sonam Wangchuk pic.twitter.com/6CO3tjZsSD — Sonam Wangchuk (@Wangchuk66) July 24, 2026

He said that even now his movement and those of his visitors has been restricted at Medanta Hospital and he is contemplating to move a contempt petition in the Delhi High Court.

He added that he managed to ensure the presence of civil society leaders from Ladakh on Thursday (July 23) night.

“I have lost 11 kgs, have no muscle mass. I was sitting there in heat and humidity. After 26-days of hunger strike, do I need to prove my sincerity,” he said.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran’s military says attacked U.S. bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait
World.content:
Iran’s military said on Friday (July 24, 2026) it carried out drone strikes against several American military facilities and bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait in retaliation for the latest U.S. attacks against the Islamic republic.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said that they targeted a data centre in Bahrain belonging to Amazon, according to state media, though neither the U.S. tech giant nor Bahrain have commented on the claim.

Watch | A Red Sea blockade could change the course of the Iran war

UN rights chief Volker Turk urged countries involved in the war to help evacuate and repatriate some 6,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz. Mr. Turk called for urgent action to remedy the plight of thousands of stranded seafarers, who are facing “a dire humanitarian and human rights crisis” in the waterway, his spokeswoman Shabia Mantoo said.

Also read | Pakistan vows retaliation against any attack on its vessels amid West Asia conflict

Several blasts sounded near Erbil airport, which hosts U.S.-led coalition troops in Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, an AFP journalist said. Explosions were heard after air defences were activated, according to the journalist who also saw drones hovering over the city, home to a major US consulate complex, and smoke rising in the airport area.

World.title: 11 naturopathy bibliographies released at KU event
World.content:
Kakatiya University, Warangal, Vice-Chancellor, K. Prathap Reddy said that naturopathy remained highly relevant in the context of present-day lifestyles and stressed the importance of adopting healthy living practices for longevity.

Speaking at the 8th anniversary celebrations of the International Naturopathy Library and Research Centre at the Kakatiya University Senate Hall on Friday, Mr. Reddy released 11 bibliography volumes on naturopathy compiled by former professor G. Rameshwaram, founder of the research centre. He also added that Kakatiya University had entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the centre to benefit research scholars.

Commending Prof. Rameshwaram’s contribution to the field, the Vice-Chancellor lauded his efforts in promoting naturopathy and creating valuable academic resources.

Prof. Rameshwaram said the bibliographies had been published in Telugu, English, Hindi and Marathi and would serve as useful reference material for naturopathy scholars worldwide. He noted that the International Naturopathy Library and Research Centre houses around 8,000 rare manuscripts, books and journals on the subject.

Telangana University Vice-Chancellor T. Yadagiri Rao appreciated Prof. Rameshwaram’s sustained efforts to promote naturopathy for improving human health.

Congratulating Prof. Rameshwaram, KU Retired Teachers’ Association president A. Sadanandam said, “Knowledge advances not by preserving old ideas unchanged, nor by rejecting them outright, but by constantly examining them in the light of new evidence.”

Kakatiya University Registrar V. Ramchandram and others attended the programme.

World.title: Pukasa holds protest meet in solidarity with Delhi students in Kerala’s Kochi
World.content:
Purogamana Kalasahithya Sangham (Pukasa), a Left-leaning collective of writers and artists, organised a protest meet in Kochi on Friday (July 24, 2026) in solidarity with the ongoing student agitation in Delhi.

Joshy Donbosco, State secretary of Pukasa, inaugurated the meet. Vanitha Sahithi State secretary Ravitha Haridas, artists Sathyapal and Sindhu Divakaran, and Pukasa district secretary Saheer Ali were among those who addressed the gathering.

A monodrama titled Hrudayam, written by Sureshkumar Sreestha, was performed by A.H. Shanavas at the event.

Salimon Kumbalangi, Thennal, and Viswan Panampukad rendered protest anthems, while Baburaj Vyttila, Anil Perumbalam, Anvar Kakkanad, Jiji Raghu, P.R. Raghu, and Aji Alath recited poems.

World.title: Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, long-time ally of Sheikh Hasina, resigns
World.content:
The President of Bangladesh, Mohammed Shahabuddin, resigned from his post on Friday (July 24, 2026). In a letter addressed to Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, Speaker of the National Assembly (Jatiyo Sansad), Mr. Shahabuddin said he was suffering from serious health issues and was unable to perform the duties of the office of President.

Mr. Shahabuddin was sworn in as the twenty-second President of Bangladesh on April 24, 2023, during the third term of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh went through a controversial election in January 2024, when Ms. Hasina was re-elected, which was followed by the uprising against her government in July-August 2024. In his letter, Mr. Shahabuddin defended his decisions that led to the formation of the interim government after the fall of Prime Minister Hasina’s government on August 5, 2024.

In the letter, he said that he is suffering from heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, and kidney complications. Earlier reports suggested that the new government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who was sworn in on February 17, 2026, was planning to appoint Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani as the next President of the country.

World.title: ‘To maintain law & order’, liquor shops in Delhi to shut by 8 pm until Sunday
World.content:
An official from one of the corporations said, “The directions have been verbally issued... all the vends and corporations will implement it immediately. An official order will be issued to all shops soon.”

Following directions from the Delhi Police Special Brach, the Excise department has decided to shut liquor shops by 8 pm for three days — Friday to Sunday. Currently, liquor shops across the city opens at 10 am and closes at 10 pm.

“The revised timings have been implemented from today. A formal order is on the way in the regard. The decision has been taken following directions from the Delhi Police,” a senior Excise department official said

“While students are protesting peacefully, some anti-social elements are trying to disrupt the protest by drinking and creating ruckus. As this can lead to untoward incidents, police requested us to revise the timings of liquor shops… it has been done,” the official added.

World.title: CWG 2026: Jadumani Singh’s 5kg gamble pays off, enters Round of 16
World.content:
Jadumani Singh had a successful 2025 – a year that was built on his southpaw excellence in the 50kg category. But the men’s boxing weight classes at major amateur events all start at the 55kg category. So the Manipuri boxer made the tough call – a five-kilogram jump in weight and the uncharted territory that comes with it would have to follow. The Commonwealth Games and its lack of seeding would have to be the first major tournament in the weight class.



The 23-year-old boxer turned in a spectacular opening round, one that set the tone for the judges over where this bout was headed, and defeated home favourite Aaron Cullen 5-0 in a unanimous win to start his Commonwealth Games campaign on Friday evening.

World.title: In new late-night video, Modi thanks students for ‘constructive’ responses
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a new video message around 11 pm on Friday, thanking students for their response to his remarks on examination paper leaks a day earlier. “Last night, I got the chance to connect with you. Thank you for the way you responded to my earlier video, with constructive suggestions,” Modi said, addressing students directly. “This bond of affection will continue. Our connection will only grow stronger from here. Thank you, thank you, friends,” he added.



The video came a day after Modi announced fast-track courts and a tougher new law to punish those behind exam paper leaks. In a video message on Thursday night, he said the government had received a draft Bill that would be taken up by the Cabinet on Friday, with provisions for fast-track courts and stricter penalties. He said the government aimed to pass the Bill in Parliament as early as the second week of the ongoing session.

World.title: Abhinandh PB’s dream run continues as Goa enter UTT final
World.content:
Manika Batra said it after losing to Syndrela Das in the league phase. It was G Sathiyan’s turn to say it for Abhinandh PB in the semi-finals. Two long-time flagbearers of Indian table tennis, doffing their hats in appreciation to the next in line after being vanquished by them.

“Extremely happy with the guy, especially being from my hometown. The way he has displayed courage to beat top players in the world, it’s a phenomenal improvement in the last few years. I think he has a great future, and hope to see him in the Indian senior team very soon,” was Sathiyan’s glowing review of Abhinandh.

The 18-year-old had just trumped his Chennai senior 11-9 and earned the winning point that took Dempo Goa Challengers into the final of Ultimate Table Tennis’ (UTT) season 7. Dabang Delhi TTC’s seventh straight semis entry, thus ended in defeat.

Abhinandh has had a sparkling start to his UTT journey. Despite playing only three matches for U Mumba in his debut season last year, he made his mark with impressive displays that helped the Mumbai-based outfit lift the trophy. He has now been promoted to a singles mainstay in Goa colours, and with four wins out of six and a finishing touch on Friday, is powering the home team’s splendid unbeaten campaign.

The teenager faced some anxious moments in the game, as Sathiyan ate up his 9-5 lead in no time to exert pressure. Abhinandh kept his calm and relied on pendulum services to seal the deal, before erupting into wild celebrations with his teammates.



Looking back at those tense moments, Abhinandh said: “I had some thoughts running in my head. I tried two shots which were unnecessary. But I did not go into a negative mindset even at 9-9, which helped me.”

He also expressed his gratitude to Sathiyan for the generous praise showered. “I respect him so much, not just in the game but personally as well. His words are very impactful to me, and being mentioned by him is an honour to me.”

How it panned out

Earlier, Alvaro Robles handed Goa the ideal start, shutting out Youssef Abdelaziz’s challenge in the opening rubber. The Spanish player kept pushing his fellow southpaw into the backhand corner and as Youssef scrambled to make his returns, his forehand side of the table kept getting exposed. After claiming the first two games with utmost ease, Robles saved three game points in the third and then snatched the golden point. Goa were three points to the good, with five more to come.



But the tie was about to get more interesting. Robles’ compatriot Maria Xiao went all out in attack to upset Goa skipper Bernadette Szocs in match 2. The win, only Maria’s second in 12 meetings with the world No. 24 Romanian, came after Szocs took the first game via a golden point. Maria retaliated with a delightful array of forehand and backhand top-spin drives to bamboozle Szocs and pull two points back for Delhi with a 10-11, 11-6, 11-4 scoreline.

It was all Goa from hereon. Robles combined with Indian TT’s rising 16-year-old sensation Syndrela to blank Sathiyan and Maria 3-0 (11-9, 11-8, 11-3) in the mixed doubles rubber, and the hosts were now just a game away from the final.



Abhinandh then stepped up, and made sure the raucous Panaji crowd has plenty to cheer for, come the title clash on Sunday.

World.title: No IOC scrutiny for Infantino over Trump’s intervention at FIFA World Cup
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has admitted that he intervened to get FIFA to allow Folarin Balogun to play the hosts' FIFA World Cup round of 16 match against Belgium. (AP Photo)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino won’t be investigated by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for US President Donald Trump’s role in overturning the suspension of an American player after he had received a red card in the previous match, the Olympic body has said. The IOC said that decisions made during the World Cup was beyond its jurisdiction and it hence cannot investigate Infantino’s alleged lack of political neutrality.

The statement comes after a complaint was made by a London-based NGO formally complained to the IOC ethics commission about Infantino. United States forward Folarin Balogun had been handed a red card in their round of 32 match against Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, the mandatory one-game ban was then overturned by FIFA. In the minutes after FIFA announced the decision, reports emerged of Trump having influenced the decision. Trump later admitted to having a conversation with Infantino over telephone to allow Balogun to play in USA’s round of 16 fixture against Belgium, which they lost 4-1.

World.title: Europe battles wildfires as heatwave forces 30,000 to evacuate across France, Spain
World.content:
Nearly 30,000 people have been evacuated from parts of France and Spain as devastating wildfires, because of the heatwave sweeping southern Europe, continue to spread quickly, according to The Guardian. Researchers have warned that soaring temperatures, dry conditions and strong winds are creating dangerous conditions, leading to wildfires. Emergency services are now struggling to contain multiple blazes.



The crisis comes as a severe marine heatwave grips the Mediterranean Sea. Climate researchers warned that “Dantesque” wildfire scenarios cannot be ruled out if extreme weather persists. A marine heatwave is declared when sea surface temperatures reach abnormally high levels.

France has requested assistance from the European Union’s Civil Protection Mechanism to tackle a major wildfire near its Atlantic coast, where the blaze has forced the evacuation of more than 18,800 people, including thousands of tourists staying at campsites and holiday homes.

World.title: Sameera Reddy recalls being told to wear bum pads: Experts on lasting impact of body shaming
World.content:
Sameera Reddy recently opened up about facing body shaming during her initial days in the film industry. “I was wearing padded bras and bum pads. Bum pads are wild. Someone said, ‘Your bum is flat’. Because at that time, it was just like a problem…so make the girl feel bad. In this case, I remember it was the assistant director who was a female. I was told to do something about it. All my outfits had built-in bras and pads. I was told on my face that how much built-in we could keep doing…do something about it…” she told Hauterrfly in an interview.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Reflecting on appearance-based workplace pressures, Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach, said that while many may dismiss these as the harsh realities of glamour, such comments reveal a much deeper psychological issue that extends far beyond films.

“As a psychotherapist, I often remind people that body shaming is rarely about the body. It is about power, acceptance and belonging. Human beings have an innate need to feel accepted by the groups they are part of. When acceptance becomes conditional upon appearance, people begin believing that who they are is somehow inadequate. Over time, this can quietly erode confidence, self-esteem and even one’s sense of identity,” remarked Delnna.

The entertainment industry may amplify these pressures because appearance is part of the profession, but similar experiences occur in everyday workplaces, schools and even within families. Someone is told they are too thin, too dark, too short, too tall, too old, too young or not attractive enough. These comments are often dismissed as “feedback” or “just being honest,” yet repeated exposure can leave deep emotional scars, she expressed.

Another important aspect of Sameera Reddy’s experience is that the criticism reportedly came from another woman. “This reminds us that body shaming is not confined to one gender. Sometimes the harshest standards are passed from one woman to another because unrealistic expectations have been normalised over generations. Hurt people can unknowingly continue the cycle of hurt unless someone consciously chooses to break it,” said Delnna.

How to build healthier relationships with our bodies?

Developing body confidence is not about pretending to love every aspect of ourselves. It is about learning to treat ourselves with dignity and respect, Delnna reflected.

Some practical steps include:



*Separate your worth from your appearance. Your kindness, character, resilience and values define you far more than any physical feature.

*Be mindful of the language you use about your own body. Self-criticism often becomes self-belief.

*Avoid comparing yourself with carefully curated images that rarely reflect real life.

*Surround yourself with people who appreciate you as a whole person rather than constantly commenting on your appearance.



*If feedback about your appearance is affecting your mental health, seek support before it begins shaping your identity.

Parents and educators also have an important role to play. “Children should grow up hearing appreciation for their effort, creativity, courage and compassion far more often than comments about weight, complexion or physical appearance. The messages they receive early in life often become the inner voice they carry into adulthood,” noted Delnna.

It does add to one’s stress (Photo: Freepik) It does add to one’s stress (Photo: Freepik)

The encouraging part of Reddy’s story is that she is speaking about it now. “When public figures openly discuss experiences of body shaming, they permit others to acknowledge similar wounds instead of silently carrying them. These conversations help shift the focus from unrealistic beauty standards to emotional well-being and self-acceptance,” expressed Delnna.

Ultimately, every profession has expectations, but no workplace should make someone believe that their value as a human being depends solely on how closely they match an ever-changing ideal.



DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

World.title: 28 Indian crew members safe after LPG tanker attacked in Iranian waters, Embassy confirms
World.content:
The Indian Embassy in Tehran on Friday confirmed that all 28 Indian crew members aboard the Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker DISHA are safe after the vessel came under attack in Iranian territorial waters.

In an official statement issued on Friday, the embassy said it was aware of the attack on the LPG tanker, identified by IMO No. 8818219, which took place earlier in the day.

“The vessel has 28 Indian crew members on board. The Embassy has been in close contact with the relevant authorities and has confirmed that all Indian crew members are safe,” the statement said.



The embassy added that it is closely monitoring the situation and remains in touch with the Iranian authorities.

Must Read | Cargo ship hit in Russian strikes in Black Sea was carrying grain: India

The statement did not provide details about the nature of the attack, the extent of damage to the vessel, or the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The confirmation comes amid heightened security concerns in the region, where commercial shipping routes have remained under close watch due to recent maritime incidents.

The attack on DISHA comes barely a few days after four Indian nationals lost their lives and another sustained critical injuries when commercial cargo vessel MV Golden Leo came under attack shortly after leaving Ukraine’s Odesa port on Sunday evening.

According to the Ministry of External Affairs, the ship had a total of 17 crew members on board, including five Indian nationals. The ministry said four of the Indian crew members were killed in the incident, while the fifth is receiving treatment and remains in critical condition.

World.title: Petrol price up by Rs3.66, HSD by Rs4.80 as govt revises fuel rates
World.content:
The government on Friday increased the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.66 and Rs4.80 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of fluctuating global oil prices following renewed hostilities in the Persian Gulf.

Following the changes, the price of petrol stands at Rs335.18 per litre, while that of HSD stands at Rs383.46 per litre. The government is charging a total of Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 25 (Saturday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.
